ai-12e898ea.vitals: HR 112 regular, BP 86/52 mmHg, RR 32/min, SpO2 89% on room air at triage and 93% on 4 L/min oxygen via nasal prongs, Temp 38.9 °C, BGL 7.8 mmol/L, CRT 4 seconds, GCS 15
ai-12e898ea.general: Older woman sitting upright in the resuscitation bay on a cardiac monitor. She is pale, diaphoretic and visibly breathless, speaking in short phrases. She is alert, oriented and tearful, and she holds her hand over her central chest.

steps.do: Observe distress, colour, work of breathing
steps.find: Pale, sweaty, tachypnoeic with accessory muscle use. Speaks 3 to 4 words at a time. Rigors noted during the examination. Alert and oriented, no new confusion.

steps.do: Feel temperature, CRT, pulse, look for stigmata
steps.find: Cool, clammy hands. CRT 4 seconds. Radial pulse 112/min, regular, low volume. No clubbing, no splinter haemorrhages, no peripheral cyanosis.

steps.do: Inspect lips and tongue, assess JVP
steps.find: Mild central cyanosis of the lips. Dry mucous membranes. JVP not elevated. No lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate apex, auscultate all areas
steps.find: Apex beat not displaced. Tachycardic, dual heart sounds, no murmur, no S3 and no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Assess expansion, tactile fremitus, percussion
steps.find: Reduced expansion on the right with splinting. Increased vocal fremitus and dullness to percussion at the right base.

steps.do: Auscultate anterior and posterior fields
steps.find: Bronchial breath sounds and coarse inspiratory crackles over the right lower zone, with a localised pleural rub at the right base. Left side clear. No wheeze.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate calves, compare circumference
steps.find: No swelling, erythema or asymmetry. Calves soft and non-tender. No pitting oedema.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate all quadrants
steps.find: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly, no pulsatile mass.

steps.do: Assess GCS, orientation, skin turgor
steps.find: GCS 15, no focal deficit. Reduced skin turgor. Urine output low since arrival.

bedside.find: 7.8 mmol/L

ai-12e898ea.key: Fever with hypotension, tachycardia and hypoxia, right basal consolidation with a pleural rub, no new confusion and no signs of a leg DVT.

ai-1337df24.vitals: HR 140, RR 40/min, Temp 36.8 °C, SpO2 98% on room air, weight 3.7 kg (birth weight 3.4 kg), CRT under 2 seconds, BGL 4.3 mmol/L
ai-1337df24.general: Alert, well-hydrated 18-day-old boy, feeding well, with normal tone and a vigorous cry. He is clearly jaundiced, but he is not drowsy, floppy or irritable.

steps.do: Observe alertness, tone, colour, cry
steps.find: Alert and active with normal tone. Jaundiced to the thighs. No pallor, bruising or petechiae. Good cry.

steps.do: Check fontanelle, mucous membranes, CRT, plot weight
steps.find: Anterior fontanelle soft and flat. Moist mucous membranes. CRT under 2 seconds. Weight 3.7 kg, above birth weight and tracking appropriately.

steps.do: Inspect sclerae, red reflex, palate, oral mucosa
steps.find: Scleral icterus. Red reflex present bilaterally with no cataract. Palate intact. No oral bleeding or petechiae. No dysmorphic features.

steps.do: Palpate femoral pulses, auscultate the heart
steps.find: Heart sounds normal with no murmur. Femoral pulses present and equal.

steps.do: Inspect work of breathing, auscultate
steps.find: No recession. Clear with equal air entry.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate liver and spleen, examine umbilicus
steps.find: Soft, non-distended. Liver edge palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin and firm. Spleen not palpable. Cord stump has separated. Umbilicus is dry and clean with no bleeding, discharge or granuloma, and no hernia.

steps.do: Inspect nappy contents and the parent's photo
steps.find: Stool pale grey-white and putty-coloured, with no blood. Urine staining the nappy dark yellow-brown. Anus normal.

steps.do: Look for bruises, petechiae, injection or heel-prick bleeding
steps.find: No bruising, petechiae or ongoing bleeding from the heel-prick sites.

steps.do: Perform Barlow and Ortolani, check abduction and leg lengths
steps.find: Barlow and Ortolani negative bilaterally. Abduction symmetrical. Leg lengths and skin creases equal.

steps.do: Assess tone, primitive reflexes, feeding behaviour
steps.find: Normal tone, symmetrical Moro and grasp reflexes, strong suck. No irritability.

bedside.find: Matches the palest cards (pale grey-white)

3.7 kg, gaining appropriately from 3.4 kg birth weight

ai-1337df24.key: Jaundice persisting beyond 2 weeks with pale putty stools, dark urine and a firm palpable liver edge in an otherwise well, thriving baby, with no bruising and no active bleeding.

ai-14bb98e4.vitals: HR 92, BP 124/76 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 37.9 °C, BGL 5.4 mmol/L, weight 78 kg
ai-14bb98e4.general: Woman who looks mildly unwell and tired, with a slightly flushed face. She is comfortable at rest, well hydrated and alert, and she protects the left breast from movement.

steps.do: Observe general appearance and comfort
steps.find: Mildly unwell and fatigued, alert and orientated. Slightly flushed. Not pale, not jaundiced. Protects the left breast when she moves.

steps.area: Breast inspection (sitting, arms by sides then raised)
steps.do: Compare both breasts for symmetry, skin and nipples
steps.find: Left breast: about 5 cm area of erythema in the retroareolar and upper inner region. Mild skin thickening with early peau d'orange over the lump. The left nipple is retracted and pulled towards the lump, new for about a month. The right breast and nipple are normal. No ulceration, no nipple rash or discharge.

steps.do: Palpate all quadrants including the tail and retroareolar region, right breast first
steps.find: Left: firm, ill-defined, tender 4 cm mass behind the nipple, partly fixed to the skin. The centre of the lump feels softer and fluctuant, and the overlying skin is warm. Right: no mass, no tenderness. No nipple discharge on gentle pressure.

steps.do: Palpate the central, anterior, posterior, lateral and apical nodes
steps.find: Left: one tender, mobile 1.5 cm node in the anterior axillary group. Right axilla: no nodes.

steps.do: Palpate nodal basins
steps.find: No supraclavicular or cervical lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Auscultate and percuss
steps.find: Clear. Equal air entry. No dullness.

steps.do: Palpate for liver and tenderness
steps.find: Soft, non-tender, no hepatomegaly.

steps.do: Percuss the thoracolumbar spine
steps.find: No bony tenderness.

bedside.find: Negative

ai-14bb98e4.key: A firm, ill-defined retroareolar mass with a fluctuant centre, new nipple retraction, early peau d'orange and a tender axillary node in a non-breastfeeding smoker who has had no response to antibiotics.

ai-26435104.vitals: HR 84, BP 116/72 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 99% on room air, Temp 36.8 °C, BGL 5.1 mmol/L, urine dipstick protein nil and glucose nil, fetal heart rate 142 bpm on Doppler
ai-26435104.general: Pale, tense and tearful woman who sits forward holding her abdomen and keeps glancing at the clock. She is alert and orientated, comfortable at rest, and calms slightly when spoken to warmly.

steps.do: Observe general appearance, oedema, distress
steps.find: Anxious, tearful, no respiratory distress. Mild non-pitting ankle swelling only. No facial oedema and no conjunctival pallor.

steps.do: Inspect the gravid abdomen, skin and fetal movements
steps.find: Gravid abdomen, longitudinal ovoid shape, linea nigra, no scars. A small fetal movement is visible during the examination.

steps.do: Measure symphysis-fundal height with a tape
steps.find: 35 cm, consistent with dates and with the normal growth scan at 32 weeks.

steps.do: Palpate fundus, lie, presentation, engagement
steps.find: Longitudinal lie, cephalic presentation, head 3/5 palpable. Fetal parts easily palpable and liquor clinically normal. Uterus soft and non-tender. No palpable tightenings.

steps.do: Auscultate with a handheld Doppler
steps.find: Fetal heart rate 142 bpm, regular. A fetal movement is felt by the patient during the check.

steps.do: Repeat BP, check reflexes and clonus, epigastric tenderness
steps.find: BP 116/72 mmHg. Reflexes normal, no clonus. No epigastric or right upper quadrant tenderness.

steps.do: Palpate calves and compare
steps.find: Soft, non-tender and symmetrical.

bedside.find: Protein nil, glucose nil
5.1 mmol/L

ai-26435104.key: Normal blood pressure and urinalysis, a fundal height consistent with dates and a fetal heart of 142 bpm on Doppler, in an anxious woman with reduced movements and a previous stillbirth. The CTG is given in Part 2.

ai-2ab0f580.vitals: HR 78, BP 118/64 (right arm), BP 120/66 (leg), RR 16, SpO2 99% on room air, temp 36.6, weight 36 kg, height 138 cm, BMI 18.9
ai-2ab0f580.general: Well, alert, interactive but shy and short for age, with a webbed neck and low posterior hairline. Proportionate build, no dysmorphic facial asymmetry, not distressed.

steps.do: Observe the child and measure height and weight
steps.find: Height 138 cm, weight 36 kg. Short with normal body proportions. Looks younger than 13 years.

steps.do: Inspect face, jaw, palate, eyes and hairline
steps.find: Low-set, slightly posteriorly rotated ears. Small lower jaw, high-arched palate. No ptosis. Epicanthic folds present. Low posterior hairline.

steps.do: Otoscopy and a simple hearing check
steps.find: Right tympanic membrane dull with mild retraction and scarring. Left has some tympanosclerosis. No active discharge. Whispered voice heard less well on the right.

steps.do: Inspect the neck and palpate the thyroid
steps.find: Webbed neck with bilateral skin folds from the mastoids to the shoulders. Thyroid not enlarged, smooth, no nodules, no tenderness. No cervical lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect chest shape and breast development (chaperone present)
steps.find: Broad, shield-shaped chest with widely spaced nipples. Breast Tanner stage 1 (no breast buds). Chest clear to auscultation with normal air entry.

steps.do: Palpate radial and femoral pulses, measure BP in right arm and leg, auscultate
steps.find: Radial and femoral pulses present, equal and no radio-femoral delay. BP 118/64 right arm and 120/66 leg, so no arm-leg gradient. Normal first and second heart sounds with a soft ejection systolic murmur at the right upper sternal edge, no radiation to the back. No heaves or thrills.

steps.do: Assess carrying angle, hands, nails and look for swelling
steps.find: Wide carrying angle (cubitus valgus) bilaterally. Short fourth metacarpals on a clenched fist. Nails slightly hyperconvex and narrow. No current hand or foot swelling.

steps.do: Inspect skin and stage pubic and axillary hair (chaperone present)
steps.find: Multiple pigmented naevi across the trunk and arms. No keloid scarring seen. Pubic hair Tanner stage 2, sparse and fine. Axillary hair minimal. External genitalia prepubertal-appearing female, no clitoromegaly.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate and auscultate
steps.find: Soft, non-tender, no masses, no organomegaly. Bowel sounds normal. No renal angle tenderness.

steps.do: Inspect the back (forward bend) and legs
steps.find: No scoliosis on forward bend. Mild genu valgum. No ankle swelling. Normal gait, normal tone and power.

bedside.find: Normal: no protein, blood, leucocytes or nitrites.

ai-2ab0f580.key: Short stature, webbed neck with low posterior hairline, widely spaced nipples, wide carrying angle, Tanner breast stage 1, a soft ejection systolic murmur, and equal arm and leg blood pressures with present femoral pulses.

ai-387d7db7.vitals: HR 108, BP 114/72, RR 20, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 35.2 °C, CRT 3 seconds, GCS 15, BGL 5.6 mmol/L
ai-387d7db7.general: Anxious, smells of alcohol, sitting upright on the trolley holding gauze to the nose. Blood-stained shirt, cool peripheries, speaking in full sentences.

steps.do: Ask the patient to speak, inspect the mouth, look at the neck
steps.find: Speaking in full sentences with a normal voice. Small amount of blood-stained saliva in the mouth, no clots, no loose teeth. No stridor, no neck swelling, no surgical emphysema, trachea midline. Mild midline neck tenderness is difficult to interpret because of alcohol and the distracting injury.

steps.do: Inspect the right neck wound
steps.find: About 5 cm oblique laceration over the right sternocleidomastoid. Dark blood oozes steadily from the wound. On deep inspiration a sucking sound is heard from the wound edges. No pulsatile bleeding, no expanding haematoma, and the platysma appears breached.

steps.do: Inspect and gently palpate the nose, midface, eyes and teeth
steps.find: Swollen, bruised, tender nose deviated to the left, with dried blood at both nostrils. No active bleeding and no clear fluid from the nose (no halo sign on the gauze). Midface stable with no steps, full eye movements with no diplopia, and the teeth occlude normally.

steps.do: Headlight and nasal speculum, suction of clots, topical decongestant, cotton bud palpation
steps.find: Once clots are suctioned, both nasal airways are blocked by a smooth, boggy, bulging red-purple swelling on each side of the septum. It does not shrink with topical decongestant, and a cotton bud shows it is soft and fluctuant, not firm like a deviated septum.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate, percuss and auscultate the chest
steps.find: Equal chest expansion, resonant to percussion, vesicular breath sounds bilaterally. No wheeze, no crepitus. SpO2 96% on room air.

steps.do: Assess perfusion, pulses, heart sounds and other bleeding
steps.find: HR 108, BP 114/72, CRT 3 seconds, cool peripheries. Heart sounds normal, no mill-wheel murmur. No other external bleeding. Abdomen soft and non-tender, pelvis stable.

steps.do: GCS, pupils, glucose, limb neurology
steps.find: GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6), pupils equal and reactive at 3 mm. BGL 5.6. Moves all limbs normally, no focal deficit.

steps.do: Fully expose, log-roll, check temperature
steps.find: Temp 35.2. Wet blood-soaked clothing. Log-roll shows no spinal step or tenderness elsewhere. No other stab wounds. Grazed right knuckles.

steps.do: Palpate the scalp and examine the ears and eyes
steps.find: No scalp haematoma or laceration, no Battle sign, no haemotympanum. Mild periorbital swelling bilaterally, no subconjunctival haemorrhage.

bedside.find: 5.6 mmol/L

ai-387d7db7.key: A right neck wound over the external jugular vein with a sucking noise on inspiration while upright, a bilateral boggy purple septal swelling, early compensated blood loss and mild hypothermia.

ai-44e14180.general: Alert, thin young man, anxious but comfortable at rest. Not jaundiced and no distress.

steps.do: Observe nutrition, colour and skin
steps.find: Slim, mildly pale, no jaundice. No spider naevi, no bruising, no tattoos or piercings, no injecting marks.

steps.do: Inspect nails and palms, check for flap
steps.find: No clubbing, no leuconychia, no palmar erythema, no Dupuytren contracture, no asterixis.

steps.do: Inspect conjunctivae and sclerae
steps.find: Mild conjunctival pallor. Sclerae anicteric. No periorbital abnormality.

steps.do: Inspect the oral cavity
steps.find: Single small aphthous ulcer on the inner lower lip. Mucous membranes moist. No candida.

steps.do: Palpate cervical, supraclavicular and axillary nodes
steps.find: No lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect, percuss and auscultate
steps.find: Clear, equal air entry, no crackles or wheeze. Respiratory pattern normal.

steps.do: Pulse, JVP and heart sounds
steps.find: Regular pulse 88/min, JVP not elevated, normal heart sounds, no murmurs, no oedema.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate, percuss and auscultate
steps.find: Mild right iliac fossa tenderness with fullness but no guarding or rebound. Liver not palpable, spleen not palpable, no ascites. Bowel sounds normal. Old healed surgical scars absent.

steps.do: Inspect the perianal skin (chaperone offered)
steps.find: Small perianal skin tag, no fistula, no abscess, no fissure.

bedside.find: Normal: no blood, protein or glucose.

ai-44e14180.key: No stigmata of chronic liver disease (no jaundice, spider naevi, palmar erythema or hepatosplenomegaly), with mild right iliac fossa tenderness and fullness and a perianal skin tag in keeping with active bowel inflammation.

ai-4f540d03.vitals: HR 170, BP 85/50, RR 40, SpO2 98% on room air, temp 36.9, CRT 3 seconds, BGL 4.1 mmol/L, weight 4.0 kg (4.4 kg at 2 weeks of age)
ai-4f540d03.general: Thin, sleepy but rousable infant who is alert when stimulated. Looks moderately dry. No respiratory distress, not jaundiced, no rash.

steps.do: Observe the infant and assess responsiveness
steps.find: Sleepy but wakes to voice and handling and is then alert, with a normal cry and good tone. Pale but not mottled or cyanosed.

steps.do: Assess work of breathing and auscultate
steps.find: Airway patent. RR 40, no recession, no grunting, no nasal flaring. Chest clear, equal air entry. SpO2 98% on room air.

steps.do: Assess HR, pulses, CRT and peripheries
steps.find: HR 170, BP 85/50. Brachial and femoral pulses present but weak-normal volume. CRT 3 seconds centrally. Extremities slightly cool. Heart sounds normal, no murmur.

steps.do: Assess fontanelle, mucous membranes, eyes, skin turgor
steps.find: Anterior fontanelle sunken. Dry mucous membranes, no tears, mildly sunken eyes. Reduced skin turgor. Weight loss of 0.4 kg from 4.4 kg (about 9%). Only 2 wet nappies in 12 hours.

steps.do: Observe the abdomen, ideally during a test feed
steps.find: Visible peristaltic waves moving left to right across the upper abdomen after the test feed. Abdomen not distended and no scars.

steps.do: Palpate gently with the infant calm and knees flexed
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. A firm, mobile, olive-shaped mass about 2 cm felt in the right upper quadrant, deep to the liver edge. No other masses, no organomegaly.

steps.do: Inspect groins and genitalia
steps.find: No inguinal hernia, testes descended and normal, no scrotal swelling.

steps.do: Inspect skin, nappy and vomitus
steps.find: No jaundice. No rash. Vomit is milky and non-bilious, with no blood. Recent stool small and pasty.

ai-4f540d03.key: Palpable olive-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant with visible left-to-right peristalsis, non-bilious projectile vomiting, and moderate dehydration (sunken fontanelle, about 9% weight loss) with compensated shock (HR 170, CRT 3 seconds, cool peripheries) and a normal BGL.

ai-7789e6bf.vitals: HR 124, BP not required, RR 44, SpO2 96% on room air, temp 37.4, weight 13 kg, CRT less than 2 seconds
ai-7789e6bf.general: Alert, playful, well hydrated toddler, interactive with the parent. Mild intermittent cough during the consultation, no drooling, no stridor, not toxic.

steps.do: Observe the child at play, colour, and posture
steps.find: Playful, normal colour, good tone, well nourished. Weight 13 kg, at about the 50th centile. No drooling, voice normal, no head tilt, no cyanosis.

steps.do: Count RR and look for distress signs
steps.find: RR 44. Mild tachypnoea only, with no subcostal or intercostal recession, no nasal flaring or grunting. SpO2 96% on room air.

steps.do: Check for clubbing, CRT and hydration
steps.find: No clubbing. CRT less than 2 seconds. Warm peripheries, moist mucous membranes, normal skin turgor.

steps.do: Observe the throat without a tongue depressor, palpate and move the neck
steps.find: Pharynx seen briefly, mildly erythematous with no bulging or asymmetry, and no drooling. Tonsils normal. Ears normal. Neck supple with full active range of movement and no torticollis, no neck swelling, no meningism. Small shotty anterior cervical nodes only.

steps.do: Inspect chest shape, expansion, and feel the trachea
steps.find: Reduced expansion on the right lower chest. Trachea and apex beat mildly shifted to the right.

steps.do: Percuss front, sides and back
steps.find: Dull to percussion at the right base posteriorly. Resonant elsewhere.

steps.do: Auscultate all zones, comparing sides
steps.find: Reduced air entry at the right base. Localised monophonic expiratory wheeze over the right lower zone. No crackles, no stridor, no bronchial breathing. Left side clear.

steps.do: Pulse, heart sounds, murmurs
steps.find: HR 124, regular, normal heart sounds, no murmur.

steps.do: Palpate abdomen and inspect skin for eczema
steps.find: Abdomen soft, non-tender, no organomegaly. No eczema, no rash.

bedside.find: 96% on room air, stable at rest.

ai-7789e6bf.key: Localised right lower zone signs (reduced expansion, dullness, reduced air entry and monophonic wheeze) with tracheal shift to the right in a well, afebrile child, with no drooling, neck stiffness or neck swelling.

ai-787441f6.vitals: HR 92, BP 102/64, RR 20, SpO2 99% on room air, Temp 36.7 C, weight 31 kg (50th centile), CRT less than 2 seconds
ai-787441f6.general: Well-grown 10-year-old boy sitting with a tablet. Alert and restless in the chair, settles with prompting, intermittently irritable and grimaces when his abdomen is touched. No dysmorphic features beyond his known condition. Not pale, not jaundiced, hydration adequate.

steps.do: Observe behaviour, nutrition, hydration and mucous membranes
steps.find: Alert, cooperative with distraction and gestures. Well grown. Mucous membranes mildly dry, normal skin turgor, no sunken eyes.

steps.do: Examine exposed skin, limbs, trunk and back for bruising or injury
steps.find: No bruises, burns, scars or patterned marks. Mild redness and callus over the knuckles of the right hand. Faint old erythema over the lower abdomen consistent with repeated pressure or striking. No rash.

steps.do: Inspect lips, gums, teeth and cheeks with torch and spatula
steps.find: Large carious lower left first molar with surrounding gingival swelling and erythema. Tender to gentle percussion with the spatula and he pulls away. Mildly enlarged, tender left submandibular lymph nodes. No facial swelling or trismus. Tongue and palate normal.

steps.do: Otoscopy and throat inspection
steps.find: Tympanic membranes normal bilaterally, canals clear. Throat not inflamed, tonsils normal.

steps.do: Inspect, auscultate heart and lungs
steps.find: Normal work of breathing, chest clear, no wheeze. Heart sounds dual, no murmurs.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate gently, percuss and auscultate, with distraction
steps.find: Mildly distended lower abdomen. Palpable firm, indentable faecal mass in the left iliac fossa extending suprapubically. Mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant with a grimace but no guarding or rebound. No organomegaly. Bowel sounds present and normal. No hernias. Bladder not palpable.

steps.do: Inspect perianal area and external genitalia, with parent present and consent
steps.find: Faecal staining of underwear and perianal skin. No fissure, no skin tags, no bruising or signs of trauma. Anal position normal. External genitalia normal. Digital rectal examination deferred in line with guidelines, as impaction is evident clinically.

steps.do: Assess tone, gait, tremor, posture, restlessness and spine
steps.find: Mild cogwheel rigidity at both wrists and elbows and a fine tremor of the hands. Mild drooling. Restless, shifting in the chair and getting up repeatedly (akathisia), settling a little with the tablet. No dystonia. Gait normal. Reflexes normal and symmetrical. Lower back inspected: no sacral dimple, tuft or lump.

steps.do: Look for pain or limitation of movement in limbs and joints
steps.find: Full range of movement in all joints, no swelling, no bone tenderness, uses all limbs normally.

ai-8b37c286.key: Distended, tympanic abdomen with tinkling bowel sounds, an empty rectum and no hernias, with a negative Murphy's sign, no fever or jaundice and signs of hypovolaemia.

steps.do: Auscultate the precordium with stethoscope (or ECG leads) for 6 seconds
steps.find: HR 70/min at birth (below 100).

steps.do: Assess CRT at sternum, peripheral colour and pulses
steps.find: CRT 4 s (prolonged). Pale and mottled peripheries. Brachial and femoral pulses weak but palpable.

steps.do: Position neutral, open airway, inspect mouth and consider suction only if obstructed
steps.find: Airway patent when head is in neutral position, no secretions or obstruction visible. Chest rise is achieved once positioning, mask seal and jaw support are correct.

steps.do: Assess tone, response to stimulation, and AVPU
steps.find: AVPU U at birth, with no response to brief stimulation.

steps.do: Measure axillary or skin temperature and ensure thermoneutral care
steps.find: 36.2 C at birth.

steps.do: Place probe on right wrist or hand (pre-ductal)
steps.find: 62% at 1 minute, with HR 70.

steps.do: Rapid check of abdomen, spine, palate, and limbs once stabilised
steps.find: Normal for a term newborn: abdomen soft with no distension, spine intact, palate intact on inspection, no obvious limb deformity or birth injury. No dysmorphic features.

bedside.find: 62% at 1 minute
36.2 C at birth

ai-fbe23e14.key: Apnoeic, floppy term newborn with HR 70 (below 100), CRT 4 seconds and SpO2 62% at 1 minute, with clear liquor and an airway that opens with neutral positioning and jaw support: needs warmth, airway positioning and positive pressure ventilation in air within the first minute, with compressions only if HR stays below 60 after 30 seconds of effective ventilation.

amsa-187.vitals: Arrival (13:10): HR 60/min regular, BP 132/84 mmHg (right arm), RR 18/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C, BGL 7.2 mmol/L, pain 7/10. After the nurse's report (13:20): HR 46/min regular, BP 96/60 mmHg, RR 20/min, SpO2 97% on room air.
amsa-187.general: 50-year-old man sitting up on the trolley, anxious, pale and sweaty, rubbing the centre of his chest. He is in obvious pain but speaks in full sentences. Alert and oriented. No xanthelasma or corneal arcus. Cardiac monitor and IV cannula in place. After the nurse's report: pale, clammy and light-headed, saying he feels faint and sick. When laid flat he feels a little less faint but stays pale and clammy.

steps.do: Feel the temperature of the hands and check capillary refill
steps.find: Warm hands, CRT 2 seconds. After the nurse's report: cool and clammy, CRT 3 seconds.

steps.do: Feel both radial pulses at the same time for rate, rhythm and radio-radial delay
steps.find: 60/min and regular, equal volume on both sides, no radio-radial delay. After the nurse's report: 46/min, regular.

steps.do: Measure the BP in the right and left arms
steps.find: Right arm 132/84, left arm 128/82, with no significant difference between arms. After the nurse's report: 96/60.

steps.do: Feel both femoral pulses
steps.find: Present and equal on both sides, with no radio-femoral delay.

steps.do: Assess the JVP with James at 45 degrees
steps.find: Not raised, 3 cm above the sternal angle. After the nurse's report: 5 cm above the sternal angle, with lungs still clear.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the praecordium, then auscultate all areas, including sitting forward for aortic regurgitation and listening for a rub
steps.find: Apex beat not displaced, no heaves or thrills. Dual heart sounds, no murmurs (no aortic or mitral regurgitation), no added sounds, no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Palpate the sternum and chest wall
steps.find: No tenderness, and pressing does not reproduce the pain.

steps.do: Check expansion, percussion and auscultation front and back
steps.find: Expansion equal on both sides, resonant to percussion throughout, vesicular breath sounds, no crackles or wheeze, no reduced breath sounds.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen, including the epigastrium, and feel for a pulsatile mass
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, no epigastric tenderness, no pulsatile or expansile mass.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the calves and ankles
steps.find: Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling, no pitting oedema.

bedside.find: Regular rhythm at 60/min on arrival. Regular rhythm at 46/min at 13:20.
7.2 mmol/L
Recorded at 13:15. The examiner hands it over in Part 2.
Sent from the cannula at 13:20 (FBC, EUC, magnesium, hs-troponin, coagulation, lipase, lipids). Results are given in Part 2.

amsa-187.key: On arrival the examination is normal, apart from a pale, sweaty man in ongoing pain. The arm BPs and the radial and femoral pulses are equal and there is no aortic regurgitation murmur, which goes against aortic dissection. There is no rub, the chest wall is not tender, the calves are normal and the lungs are clear, which goes against pericarditis, a musculoskeletal cause, PE and heart failure. The new bradycardia (46) and hypotension (96/60), with cool peripheries, a JVP that has risen to 5 cm and clear lungs, suggest an inferior (right coronary artery) infarct affecting the AV node and possibly the right ventricle. This needs a senior at the bedside now, defibrillator pads and a repeat rhythm strip, and nitrates must be avoided.

amsa-188.vitals: HR 96 beats/min regular, BP 150/90 mmHg right arm (146/88 mmHg left arm if both arms checked), RR 20 breaths/min, SpO2 96% on room air, temperature 36.7°C, alert, pain 7/10
amsa-188.general: Overweight man lying propped up at 45 degrees. He is pale, sweaty and anxious, in moderate discomfort, and keeps holding and rubbing the centre of his chest. Not cachectic, no visible oedema, no features of Marfan syndrome.

steps.do: Inspect and feel both hands for temperature, clubbing, splinter haemorrhages, Osler's nodes, Janeway lesions, tar staining, peripheral cyanosis and tendon xanthomata; check capillary refill.
steps.find: Cool and clammy. Tar staining of the right index and middle fingers. Capillary refill 2 seconds. No clubbing, splinter haemorrhages, Osler's nodes, Janeway lesions, peripheral cyanosis or tendon xanthomata.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm, volume and character; check for radio-radial and radio-femoral delay; feel both femoral pulses.
steps.find: Radial pulse 96 beats/min, regular, normal volume and character. No radio-radial or radio-femoral delay. Femoral pulses equal.

steps.do: Feel the carotid pulse character, listen for carotid bruits and measure the JVP at 45 degrees.
steps.find: Carotid pulses normal in character, no bruits. JVP 2 cm above the sternal angle (normal).

steps.do: Inspect the eyes for corneal arcus, xanthelasma and conjunctival pallor and check the pupils; inspect the lips and tongue for central cyanosis, the teeth, the palate and the cheeks for malar flush.
steps.find: Bilateral corneal arcus. No xanthelasma or conjunctival pallor. Pupils equal and reactive. No central cyanosis, fair dentition, normal palate, no malar flush.

steps.do: Inspect for scars, a pacemaker, visible pulsations, chest deformity and the breathing pattern; palpate the apex beat, for a left parasternal heave and for thrills over each valve area.
steps.find: No scars, pacemaker, visible pulsations or chest deformity. Breathing slightly fast, no accessory muscle use. Apex beat in the 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line, not displaced, normal character. No heaves or thrills.

steps.do: Listen over all four valve areas and time with the carotid pulse; roll him to the left lateral position for the mitral area and sit him forward in expiration for the aortic and pulmonary areas.
steps.find: S1 and S2 heard and normal. No added sounds, murmurs or pericardial rub, including in the left lateral position and sitting forward in expiration. No aortic regurgitation murmur.

steps.do: Percuss and auscultate the chest, including the bases, for crackles or effusion.
steps.find: Resonant throughout, vesicular breath sounds, no crackles or effusion.

steps.do: Palpate for the liver and spleen, check for ascites, and palpate and auscultate the abdominal aorta.
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No hepatomegaly, splenomegaly or ascites. Abdominal aorta not palpably expansile, no bruits.

steps.do: Check for pitting oedema, feel the peripheral pulses, inspect the calves, the Achilles tendons for xanthomata, the skin and hair, and the toes for clubbing.
steps.find: No pitting oedema. Peripheral pulses present and equal. No calf swelling or tenderness. No Achilles tendon xanthomata, normal hair and colour, no clubbing of the toes.

bedside.find: Requested from the practice nurse: "I'll record it now." The tracing (recorded at 10:12) is handed over in Part 2.
Right arm 150/90 mmHg, left arm 146/88 mmHg. No significant difference between the arms.
6.4 mmol/L

amsa-188.key: The cardiovascular examination is essentially normal, apart from signs of acute illness (pale, sweaty, cool and clammy, slightly fast breathing) and risk-factor signs (tar staining and corneal arcus). This fits ongoing ischaemic chest pain, so the urgent step is a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Equal arm pressures, normal pulses with no radio-femoral delay and no aortic regurgitation murmur make aortic dissection less likely. A normal JVP, clear lungs and no new murmur mean there is no sign of heart failure or mechanical complications, and with systolic BP above 90 mmHg and SpO2 of 96% on room air, GTN is safe and oxygen is not needed.

amsa-189.vitals: HR 86 beats/min regular, BP 140/82 mmHg, RR 18/min, SpO2 95% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C (10:05, seated at rest)
amsa-189.general: Thin older man sitting comfortably at rest. He speaks in full sentences with a hoarse, croaky voice and has an occasional dry cough after walking in from the waiting room. No increased work of breathing, no cyanosis and no obvious pallor. Alert and oriented. Weight 68 kg, height 178 cm (BMI 21.5). The practice record shows 74 kg eight months ago, a loss of 6 kg (about 8%).

steps.do: Look for clubbing, nicotine staining, peripheral cyanosis and wasting of the small muscles of the hand. Test grip strength and sensation in the hands (C8 and T1 involvement from an apical tumour).
steps.find: No clubbing, no nicotine staining, no peripheral cyanosis. No wasting of the small hand muscles. Grip strength normal on both sides. Sensation normal in both hands.

steps.do: Look for ptosis and compare the pupils for Horner's syndrome. Look for facial swelling or plethora (superior vena cava obstruction) and central cyanosis.
steps.find: No ptosis. Pupils equal and reactive to light, so no Horner's syndrome. No facial swelling or plethora. No central cyanosis.

steps.do: Check the tracheal position and the JVP, look for distended neck veins, and palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes.
steps.find: Trachea midline. JVP not raised and neck veins not distended. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect the chest shape, scars and work of breathing, then assess chest expansion front and back.
steps.find: Normal chest shape with no scars or dilated veins over the chest wall. Expansion symmetrical.

steps.do: Percuss front and back, comparing sides and including the apices above the clavicles and the clavicles themselves.
steps.find: Dull over the right apex, above the clavicle and in the first and second intercostal spaces anteriorly. Resonant everywhere else.

steps.do: Listen front, back and axillae, including the apices, for breath sounds, added sounds and vocal resonance.
steps.find: Breath sounds and vocal resonance reduced over the right apex. Vesicular breath sounds elsewhere. No crackles (in particular no fine bibasal crackles), no wheeze, no pleural rub.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and check for ankle and sacral oedema to screen for heart failure.
steps.find: Heart sounds dual with no murmurs. No ankle or sacral oedema.

steps.do: Palpate for hepatomegaly as a sign of metastatic spread.
steps.find: Abdomen soft and non-tender. No hepatomegaly.

steps.do: Palpate and percuss the spine and ribs for tenderness that could suggest bony spread.
steps.find: No spinal or rib tenderness.

bedside.find: 68 kg, height 178 cm, BMI 21.5. Down from 74 kg eight months ago, an unintentional loss of about 8%.
6.1 mmol/L (random), normal
Sinus rhythm at 86 beats/min, normal axis and intervals. No ischaemic changes and no left ventricular hypertrophy.
No blood, protein, glucose, leucocytes or nitrites

amsa-189.key: The important findings are dullness to percussion and reduced breath sounds over the right apex, together with an objective 6 kg (about 8%) weight loss and a hoarse voice. In an older man exposed to asbestos, this suggests a right apical mass, possibly a superior sulcus tumour. The important negatives are no Horner's syndrome, no hand wasting, no supraclavicular nodes and no signs of SVC obstruction, which point against obvious local spread. The absence of clubbing, fine bibasal crackles, raised JVP and oedema points away from asbestosis and heart failure.

amsa-190.vitals: RR 14/min, SpO2 98% on room air, HR 70/min regular, BP 128/80 mmHg lying, temperature 36.6 °C, capillary glucose 5.4 mmol/L; no postural drop on standing
amsa-190.general: Well-looking 55-year-old woman, comfortable and sitting steadily in the chair. She is between attacks and not currently vertiginous. She is not pale, not distressed and not vomiting. She seems anxious but is fully alert and talking normally.

steps.do: Inspect both pinnae, the skin behind the ears and the canal openings for scars, deformity and discharge.
steps.find: Normal pinnae on both sides. No scars and no discharge.

steps.do: Look into both ear canals and at both tympanic membranes with an otoscope.
steps.find: Both ear canals are clear. Both tympanic membranes are intact and pearly grey with a normal light reflex. No fluid or retraction on either side.

steps.do: Whisper number and letter combinations into each ear while masking the other ear by rubbing the tragus.
steps.find: Hearing is reduced on the right, where she misses most of the combinations. Normal on the left.

steps.do: Rinne in each ear, comparing air with bone conduction (mastoid); Weber with the fork on the vertex or forehead.
steps.find: Rinne is positive in both ears: air conduction is louder than bone. Weber lateralises to the left. Together this means a right sensorineural hearing loss.

steps.do: Look for spontaneous nystagmus in primary gaze, then test smooth pursuit in an H pattern, watching for gaze-evoked nystagmus and asking about double vision. Head impulse test to each side if performed.
steps.find: No spontaneous or gaze-evoked nystagmus. Eye movements are full with smooth pursuit and no double vision. Head impulse test is normal to both sides, with no corrective saccade.

steps.area: Cranial nerves V and VII (and the rest)
steps.do: Facial light touch in V1, V2 and V3 on both sides, corneal reflex, and facial movements (raise eyebrows, screw eyes shut, puff out cheeks, show teeth). Screen the remaining cranial nerves.
steps.find: Facial sensation is normal and symmetrical in all three divisions. Corneal reflex present on both sides. Facial movements are full and symmetrical. The other cranial nerves are normal.

steps.do: Tone, power, reflexes and sensation in the upper and lower limbs.
steps.find: Tone, power, reflexes and sensation are normal and symmetrical in all four limbs.

steps.do: Finger-nose test, rapid alternating movements and heel-shin test on both sides.
steps.find: Finger-nose, rapid alternating movements and heel-shin are normal on both sides. No dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesis or intention tremor.

steps.do: Normal gait, heel-to-toe (tandem) walking, Romberg test, and Unterberger stepping test if performed.
steps.find: Gait is normal, including heel-to-toe walking. Romberg negative. Unterberger shows no significant rotation.

steps.do: Do or offer the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre to the right and to the left, watching for nystagmus and asking about vertigo. (Low yield, because her vertigo is not positional.)
steps.find: No nystagmus and no vertigo on either side. Negative on both sides.

bedside.find: 128/80 mmHg lying after 5 minutes' rest, 124/82 mmHg (HR 78) at 1 minute standing and 126/80 mmHg (HR 76) at 3 minutes standing. No symptoms on standing. No postural drop.
5.4 mmol/L (normal).
Pulse is regular. Heart sounds are dual with no murmur. No carotid bruits.

amsa-190.key: The normal otoscopy, positive Rinne on both sides and Weber lateralising to the left point to a right sensorineural hearing loss, which fits her fluctuating right-sided hearing loss, tinnitus and fullness. There is no nystagmus, the cranial nerves, cerebellar signs and gait are normal, and Dix-Hallpike is negative, so a central (posterior circulation) cause and BPPV are unlikely. Normal observations with no postural drop exclude presyncope. Together these support an inner ear cause such as Ménière's disease, which the audiogram will need to confirm.

amsa-194.vitals: 08:00 set: Temp 36.9 °C, HR 88 beats/min regular, BP 128/78 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air, pain 6/10, weight 84 kg
amsa-194.general: Alert, tired-looking man of normal build sitting up in bed, holding his hands carefully in his lap. No Cushingoid features, no bruising or thin skin. No splints or walking aids in use (he has old wrist splints at home).

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae, sclerae, face, scalp and mouth
steps.find: Mild conjunctival pallor. No scleritis, episcleritis or iritis. No malar rash, alopecia or mouth ulcers.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the extensor surfaces of the elbows and forearms; ask him to raise both arms above his head
steps.find: No nodules, no rash, no psoriatic plaques at the elbows. Full range of shoulder movement with mild discomfort in both shoulders.

steps.do: Hands resting on a pillow, rings and watch off, arms exposed to the elbows; inspect the dorsal surfaces of both hands, including the nails
steps.find: In both hands the fingers angle towards the little finger at the knuckles, and the bases of the fingers sit lower than the knuckles. Right index and middle fingers and left middle finger: middle joint bent backwards, end joint bent down. Both thumbs: bent at the base knuckle and bent backwards at the end joint. Visible swelling of both wrists, the 2nd and 3rd knuckles of both hands and several middle finger joints. Firm lumps over the backs of several middle finger joints and knuckles. Hollowing between the long bones on the back of both hands. DIP joints look normal, with no swelling or bony enlargement and no Heberden's nodes. Nails normal: no pitting, ridging, onycholysis or hyperkeratosis. No scars, rash, bruising, nail-fold infarcts or tophi. Skin not tight or shiny; no dactylitis.

steps.do: Turn the hands over and inspect the palms
steps.find: Mild redness of the palms over the base of the thumb and the little finger. No thenar wasting. No palmar crease pallor. No Raynaud's changes or digital ulcers.

steps.do: After asking about pain, check temperature, then gently palpate the wrists, MCPs, PIPs and DIPs, do a gentle MCP squeeze, feel the lumps, and ask him to make a fist
steps.find: Both wrists, the 2nd and 3rd MCP joints of both hands, the right 2nd and 3rd PIPs and the left 3rd PIP are tender, warm, with soft, spongy swelling. Squeezing across the knuckles is painful in both hands. The lumps are firm, rubbery, mobile and non-tender. DIP joints are normal. Fist incomplete in both hands, fingertips 2 cm short of the palm.

steps.do: Assess active and passive wrist flexion and extension; try to correct the finger and thumb deformities passively
steps.find: Wrist flexion and extension reduced to about 40° each way, painful at the end of range, with crepitus. The angling of the fingers at the knuckles and the bent finger and thumb deformities do not straighten when passive correction is attempted.

steps.do: Tinel's and Phalen's tests on both sides; light touch in median, ulnar and radial distributions
steps.find: Tinel's and Phalen's tests negative on both sides. Sensation normal in the median, ulnar and radial distributions.

steps.do: Test thumb flexion, extension, abduction and opposition; grip, pinch and key grip; ask him to do up a button, write a sentence and open a jar
steps.find: All thumb movements present but weak. Grip, pinch and key grip weak on both sides. He struggles to do up a button, writes slowly and untidily, and cannot open a jar.

steps.area: Feet, other joints and cervical spine
steps.do: MTP squeeze and inspection of the feet; screen the elbows, shoulders, knees and ankles; examine neck movement and do a brief limb neuro screen
steps.find: MTP squeeze tender on both sides, with swelling across the forefoot. No callosities or ulcers. Elbows, shoulders, knees and ankles: no effusion or synovitis. Neck rotation mildly reduced, not tender. Arm and leg power, sensation and reflexes normal.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and lungs, check for lymphadenopathy and palpate for the spleen
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmur, no pericardial rub. Chest clear, no fine crackles. No lymphadenopathy. Spleen not palpable.

bedside.find: 5.8 mmol/L (random), normal: a useful baseline before a corticosteroid course
No blood, protein, leucocytes or nitrites; glucose negative
6/10 at rest, worse with hand movement; 8/10 at worst first thing in the morning

amsa-194.key: He has symmetrical, warm, boggy synovitis of the wrists, MCPs, PIPs and MTPs with the DIPs spared, which is an active inflammatory flare and not bony osteoarthritic swelling. He also has fixed ulnar deviation with MCP subluxation, swan neck deformities, Z-thumbs, rheumatoid nodules and interosseous wasting, all signs of long-standing, damaging rheumatoid arthritis. Normal nails, skin and DIPs, no tophi, fixed rather than correctable deformities, no fever and no single joint out of proportion all point away from psoriatic arthritis, gout, SLE (Jaccoud's) and septic arthritis, while the weak grip and poor hand function show how much the flare is disabling him.

amsa-195.vitals: BP 130/85 mmHg, HR 105/min irregularly irregular, RR 18/min, Temp 37.0 °C, SpO2 98% on room air, weight 56 kg, height 168 cm, BMI 19.8 kg/m²
amsa-195.general: Thin young woman who is restless and fidgety and talks quickly. She is wearing a light singlet on a cool day when others are in jumpers. She is not short of breath at rest, is alert and oriented, and is comfortable sitting on a chair with her neck and arms exposed.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands for temperature and sweating, and look at the palms and nails for palmar erythema, onycholysis, clubbing, thyroid acropachy and palmar crease pallor.
steps.find: Warm and moist (sweaty) hands. Mild palmar erythema. Onycholysis of both ring fingernails. No clubbing or thyroid acropachy. No palmar crease pallor. Nails not brittle.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate and rhythm. Test for tremor with the arms held out (with a sheet of paper laid on the hands). Test the biceps and supinator reflexes. Do Pemberton's sign with both arms raised above the head for 1 minute.
steps.find: Pulse 105/min and irregularly irregular. Fine tremor with the arms held out; the paper trembles. Biceps and supinator reflexes are brisk. Pemberton's sign is negative: no facial plethora or distress with the arms raised.

steps.do: Inspect from the front, the side and from above and behind for exophthalmos. Look for lid retraction, test for lid lag, and look for conjunctival redness, chemosis and whether the eyes close fully. Test eye movements with an H pattern, asking about double vision and pain. Check visual acuity and colour vision. Look at the outer eyebrows, the scalp hair and the conjunctivae for pallor.
steps.find: Exophthalmos in both eyes: sclera visible below the iris, and the eyes stick out past the brow when viewed from above and from the side. Lid retraction (sclera visible above the iris) with a staring look. Lid lag present when following a finger downwards. Mild conjunctival redness, no chemosis, and the eyes close fully. Eye movements full in all directions, with no double vision and no pain on movement. Visual acuity 6/6 in each eye; colour vision normal. Outer eyebrows and scalp hair normal. No conjunctival pallor.

steps.do: Inspect the front of the neck for swelling, scars, redness and distended veins. Ask her to take a sip of water and swallow, then to stick out her tongue.
steps.find: A visible, diffuse, symmetrical swelling in the front of the neck, about two to three times normal size. No scars, redness or distended veins. It moves up when she swallows. It does not move when she sticks out her tongue.

steps.do: Palpate the thyroid from behind (and then from the front), with a swallow. Describe the size, symmetry, consistency, tenderness, any nodules and the lower border. Check the position of the trachea and palpate the cervical lymph nodes.
steps.find: Both lobes and the isthmus are diffusely and symmetrically enlarged. The gland is smooth, soft to firm and non-tender, with no discrete nodule. The lower border can be felt on swallowing. Trachea central. No cervical lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Percuss over the manubrium for retrosternal extension and listen over both thyroid lobes for a bruit.
steps.find: Resonant over the manubrium, so no retrosternal extension. A soft bruit over both lobes.

steps.do: Listen to the heart, assess the JVP and listen to the lung bases for signs of heart failure.
steps.find: Heart sounds dual and irregular, with no murmur. JVP not raised. Chest clear.

steps.do: Inspect the shins for pretibial myxoedema and the ankles for oedema. Test for proximal myopathy by asking her to stand from a chair with her arms folded. Test the knee and ankle reflexes.
steps.find: No pretibial myxoedema. No ankle oedema. She stands from the chair with her arms folded, a little slowly but without help. Knee and ankle reflexes are brisk.

bedside.find: 5.8 mmol/L (normal)
No protein, blood, glucose, ketones, leucocytes or nitrites
Negative
Recorded by the practice nurse. She is haemodynamically stable. The ECG is handed over with her blood results in Part 2.

amsa-195.key: Eliza has a diffuse, smooth, non-tender goitre with a bruit and no nodule. She also has signs of thyrotoxicosis: warm sweaty hands, fine tremor, brisk reflexes and onycholysis. Together with exophthalmos, lid retraction and lid lag, this points strongly to Graves' disease with orbitopathy rather than nodular disease or thyroiditis. Her pulse is irregularly irregular at 105/min, which suggests thyrotoxic atrial fibrillation; she is haemodynamically stable with no heart failure, and the ECG will confirm the rhythm. She has no pressure symptoms or signs (resonant manubrium, negative Pemberton's sign, trachea central), and her vision, colour vision and eye movements are all normal, so there is no sign of optic nerve damage or eye muscle restriction (no optic neuropathy or restrictive myopathy).

amsa-196.vitals: HR 110 bpm regular, BP 128/78 mmHg, RR 18 breaths/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 37.2 °C, BGL 6.4 mmol/L
amsa-196.general: Unwell, pale and in obvious pain on the trolley. She shifts about and draws her knees up with each wave of pain, then settles between waves. Alert and talking in full sentences. The emesis bag beside the bed holds bilious and faeculent (brown, foul-smelling) material.

steps.do: Inspect the hands, face and eyes for stigmata of chronic liver disease, pallor and jaundice. Palpate the supraclavicular fossae for lymph nodes, especially the left (Virchow's node).
steps.find: No stigmata of chronic liver disease. No jaundice. No supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect the mucous membranes, measure central capillary refill time and feel the peripheries.
steps.find: Dry mucous membranes. CRT 2 seconds. Peripheries warm.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and the lung fields.
steps.find: Heart sounds dual, no murmurs, rhythm regular. Chest clear with good air entry both sides. Normal.

steps.do: Expose the abdomen and inspect it for distension, scars, visible masses and visible peristalsis.
steps.find: Obviously distended. Three small, well-healed laparoscopic scars (umbilical, right iliac fossa and left iliac fossa).

steps.do: Palpate gently, starting away from the worst pain and watching her face, for tenderness, guarding, rigidity, rebound tenderness and masses.
steps.find: Tender throughout. No guarding, rigidity or rebound tenderness. No masses. No organomegaly.

steps.do: Percuss all regions of the abdomen.
steps.find: Tympanic throughout.

steps.do: Auscultate for bowel sounds.
steps.find: Tinkling bowel sounds present.

steps.do: Examine the inguinal, femoral and umbilical regions and each laparoscopic port site, including a cough impulse.
steps.find: No inguinal, femoral, umbilical or port-site hernia. Cough impulse negative.

steps.do: Explain the examination, obtain consent and ask for a chaperone. Perform a PR examination.
steps.find: Empty rectum. No blood on the glove. No mass.

bedside.find: 6.4 mmol/L
Sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm, normal axis, normal intervals. No AF and no ischaemic changes.
Not available because she has not passed urine since arrival.
Small residual volume. The bladder is nearly empty, which fits poor urine output from dehydration rather than retention.

amsa-196.key: The findings that matter are a distended, tympanic abdomen with tinkling bowel sounds, laparoscopic scars, normal hernial orifices and an empty rectum. Together with the faeculent vomiting, these point to a mechanical distal small bowel obstruction, most likely from adhesions after her previous laparoscopy. She is tachycardic with dry mucous membranes and has not passed urine, so she is significantly fluid depleted. There is no guarding, rigidity or rebound and she is afebrile, so there are no signs of peritonism or strangulation yet, but this must be reassessed regularly.

amsa-197.vitals: HR 72/min regular, BP 136/84 mmHg (right and left arm similar), RR 14/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C, weight 85 kg, height 177 cm, BMI 27 kg/m²
amsa-197.general: Well and comfortable at rest, sitting without distress, not in pain during the consultation. Not pale, not jaundiced, not sweaty. Looks a little tired and stressed. Overweight (BMI 27).

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for clubbing, koilonychia, palmar pallor and stigmata of chronic liver disease; feel the radial pulse.
steps.find: No clubbing, koilonychia or palmar pallor. No palmar erythema or other stigmata of chronic liver disease. Radial pulse 72/min, regular.

steps.do: Pull down the lower eyelid to look at the conjunctivae and the sclerae; look at the mouth.

amsa-197.key: The examination is reassuring. There are no ALARM signs: no pallor, no jaundice, no Virchow's node, no epigastric mass, no melaena on rectal examination. There are also no signs of a cardiac, aortic or biliary cause: normal heart sounds, equal pulses with similar BP in both arms, no pulsatile mass, and Murphy's sign is negative. The abdomen is soft and non-tender even in the epigastrium, which fits uncomplicated peptic ulcer disease between episodes. The only abnormal findings are a BMI of 27, which is overweight, and crepitus in his left knee from the osteoarthritis that explains his long-term ibuprofen use.

amsa-199.vitals: HR 105/min regular, BP 130/80 mmHg, RR 14/min, Temp 37.8 °C, SpO2 99% on room air, weight 64 kg
amsa-199.general: Tired, uncomfortable young woman sitting up on the trolley and leaning forward. She won't lie back. She is slightly flushed and speaking in full sentences, with no increased work of breathing. Not pale, not clammy and not cyanosed. Alert and orientated.

steps.find: Right arm 130/80 mmHg, left arm 128/78 mmHg, so equal in both arms. No pulsus paradoxus (fall of less than 10 mmHg on inspiration).

steps.find: JVP not raised, with no rise on inspiration. No surgical emphysema in the neck. Trachea central.

A scratchy, high-pitched, superficial sound at the left lower sternal edge, heard best sitting forward in held expiration. It persists when she holds her breath. Lying her back makes the pain worse (8/10) and it eases when she sits forward again.

steps.do: Assess tracheal position, chest expansion and percussion, and auscultate the lung fields front and back.
steps.find: Trachea central, expansion equal and percussion resonant on both sides. Vesicular breath sounds throughout, with no crackles, wheeze or pleural rub.

steps.do: Palpate the sternum, costochondral junctions and ribs. Inspect the chest wall for a rash or vesicles, and feel for surgical emphysema.
steps.find: No chest wall tenderness, and pressing does not reproduce the pain. No rash or vesicles in any dermatome. No surgical emphysema.

steps.do: Palpate all regions, including the epigastrium.
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, including the epigastrium. No guarding and no organomegaly.

steps.find: Calves soft and non-tender, with no swelling and equal calf size. No ankle oedema.

steps.find: No joint swelling or tenderness and no rash.

amsa-199.key: The scratchy, superficial sound at the left lower sternal edge that persists in held expiration is a pericardial friction rub. Together with sharp, pleuritic chest pain that is worse lying flat and better sitting forward, it strongly suggests acute pericarditis. There are no signs of tamponade: BP is stable, there is no pulsus paradoxus, the JVP is not raised and the heart sounds are not muffled. BP is equal in both arms (against dissection), the chest examination is normal with no surgical emphysema (against pneumothorax and oesophageal rupture), and the calves are normal with SpO2 99% (making PE less likely). The temperature of 37.8 °C and HR of 105 fit an inflammatory, probably viral, process, and her temperature is still below the 38 °C high-risk threshold.

amsa-200.vitals: HR 104 beats/min regular, BP 156/88 mmHg, RR 22/min, SpO2 94% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C, weight 70 kg (67 kg in the practice record 3 months ago)
amsa-200.general: Older woman sitting upright in the chair. She is mildly breathless at rest and pauses for breath mid-sentence. Not cyanosed, not pale, not distressed. Alert and oriented.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands for perfusion, clubbing, nicotine staining and tremor, and check capillary refill.
steps.find: Warm hands with capillary refill under 2 seconds. No clubbing, no nicotine staining, no tremor.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and character.
steps.find: Rate 104 beats/min, regular, normal character.

steps.do: Look for conjunctival pallor, central cyanosis, lid lag and exophthalmos.
steps.find: No conjunctival pallor, no central cyanosis, no lid lag or exophthalmos.

steps.do: Sit her at 45 degrees and measure the JVP, test the hepatojugular reflux, and feel the carotid pulse for volume and upstroke.
steps.find: JVP raised 5 cm above the sternal angle, with a positive hepatojugular reflux. Carotid pulse normal in volume and upstroke (not slow-rising).

steps.do: Check the position of the trachea and look and feel for a goitre.
steps.find: Trachea midline. No goitre.

steps.find: Apex beat displaced to the 6th intercostal space, anterior axillary line. No heave or thrill. S1 and S2 with a third heart sound (S3 gallop). No murmurs: no ejection systolic murmur and nothing radiating to the carotids.

steps.do: Assess expansion, percuss, and auscultate all zones front and back.
steps.find: Expansion reduced at both bases. Dull to percussion at both bases, stony dull at the lowest part. Reduced breath sounds at both bases, with fine end-inspiratory crackles in both lower zones extending to the mid zones. No wheeze, no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Palpate for hepatomegaly and right upper quadrant tenderness.
steps.find: Soft. Liver edge not palpable, no right upper quadrant tenderness.

steps.do: Press for pitting oedema at the ankles, shins and sacrum, and look at the calves for swelling or tenderness.
steps.find: No pitting oedema of the ankles, shins or sacrum. Calves soft, non-tender and equal in size.

bedside.test: Weight compared with the practice record
bedside.find: 70 kg today, up from 67 kg 3 months ago (3 kg gain), which fits fluid retention.

amsa-200.key: At rest she has a fast heart rate (HR 104), fast breathing (RR 22) and borderline oxygen (SpO2 94%), and she has gained 3 kg. Together with orthopnoea and PND, this points to fluid overload. The raised JVP with positive hepatojugular reflux, displaced apex, S3, bibasal crackles reaching the mid zones and stony dull bases point to congestive heart failure with pulmonary oedema and bilateral pleural effusions, most likely after her NSTEMI. There is no murmur, the carotid upstroke is normal, there is no wheeze and the calves are normal, which makes aortic stenosis, COPD and PE less likely. There is no peripheral oedema.

amsa-201.vitals: RR 26/min, SpO2 93% on room air, HR 110/min regular, BP 124/76 mmHg, Temp 36.8 °C, pain 7/10 (triage 20 minutes ago: RR 24/min, SpO2 93% RA, HR 106/min, BP 128/78 mmHg)

Not cyanosed, not pale, not sweaty. No obvious Marfanoid habitus.

steps.find: None. Arm span not greater than height, palate not high-arched, no joint hypermobility, no pectus or other chest wall deformity.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume, and check the blood pressure
steps.find: Pulse 110/min, regular, good volume. BP 124/76 mmHg, maintained.

steps.do: Look at the JVP with him sitting up and feel the trachea
steps.find: JVP not raised. Trachea central.

steps.do: Expose and inspect the chest front and back, looking for trauma, deformity and symmetry of movement
steps.find: No bruising, wounds or deformity. Mild use of accessory muscles. Less movement of the left chest wall.

steps.do: Palpate for tenderness and surgical emphysema, assess expansion front and back, and locate the apex beat
steps.find: Chest wall not tender. No surgical emphysema. Expansion reduced on the left. Apex beat in the normal position (5th intercostal space, midclavicular line), not displaced.

steps.do: Percuss both sides from apex to base, front, sides and back, comparing side to side
steps.find: Hyper-resonant over the whole left chest. Right chest resonant throughout.

steps.find: Markedly reduced breath sounds over the left chest, with reduced vocal resonance on the left. Vesicular breath sounds on the right. No wheeze, no crackles, no pleural rub.

steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, no pericardial rub.

steps.find: Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling or oedema in either leg.

bedside.find: Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 110/min, looks like sinus tachycardia. No ectopics or arrhythmia seen.

amsa-201.key: The left side has reduced expansion, hyper-resonance, and markedly reduced breath sounds and vocal resonance, while the right side is normal. In a tall young male smoker with sudden breathlessness and left pleuritic pain, this points strongly to a large left pneumothorax. There are no signs of tension: the trachea is central, BP is maintained, the JVP is not raised, the apex beat is not displaced and the peripheries are warm. However, RR and HR are rising and SpO2 is 93% on room air, so he needs senior review and close reassessment for tension. Soft, non-tender calves and a normal right lung with no wheeze or rub make PE, asthma and pericarditis less likely.

amsa-202.vitals: RR 28/min, SpO2 93% on room air (94% at triage), HR 114/min regular (sinus tachycardia on monitor), BP 126/76 mmHg, Temp 37.2 °C, alert (AVPU A), CRT under 2 seconds, Height 178 cm, Weight 75 kg

steps.find: Resonant throughout and equal on both sides. No hyper-resonance on one side and no dullness.

steps.do: Auscultate both lung fields front and back, comparing sides
steps.find: Breath sounds present and equal on both sides. Widespread high-pitched polyphonic expiratory wheeze with a prolonged expiratory phase. No crackles, no bronchial breathing. Not a silent chest.

amsa-202.key: Terry has severe acute asthma: he cannot complete sentences, is using accessory muscles with recession and a tracheal tug, and his SpO2 is 93% on room air and falling, so he needs a bronchodilator by spacer and senior help now. There are no life-threatening features: he is alert, not exhausted or cyanosed, wheeze is clearly audible (not a silent chest) and SpO2 is above 90%. A central trachea with resonance and air entry equal on both sides makes pneumothorax unlikely. The absence of fever, crackles and urticaria argues against pneumonia and anaphylaxis, and the monitor shows regular sinus tachycardia rather than an arrhythmia.

amsa-203.vitals: Temperature 38.3 °C, HR 104 beats/min regular, RR 22/min, SpO2 95% on room air, BP 128/76 mmHg, weight 68 kg (practice nurse set at 09:40)

steps.find: Trachea central. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

amsa-203.key: The left lower zone shows the signs of consolidation: dullness, bronchial breathing, coarse crackles and increased vocal resonance. Below this, at the very left base, stony dullness with reduced breath sounds and reduced vocal resonance points to a small effusion. Together with fever, tachycardia, tachypnoea and rusty sputum, this fits left lower lobe pneumonia with a parapneumonic effusion. She is alert, her BP is normal, her RR is below 30 and her SpO2 is 95% on room air, and her calves and cardiovascular examination are normal. So nothing here points to severe illness, PE or heart failure, and she is mildly dry.

amsa-204.vitals: Temp 37.8 °C, HR 92 beats/min regular, BP 112/70 mmHg, RR 18/min, SpO2 97% on room air (taken 10:20); weight 50 kg (55 kg 2 months ago by her report), height 160 cm, BMI 19.5

steps.find: Coarse crackles over the right upper zone, anteriorly below the right clavicle and posteriorly above the right scapula. No bronchial breathing and no wheeze. Vocal resonance normal. Left lung and right base clear.

steps.do: Assess the JVP, auscultate the heart and check for peripheral oedema
steps.find: JVP not raised. Heart sounds dual, no murmurs. No peripheral oedema.

steps.find: Calves soft, non-tender and equal in size. No signs of DVT.

steps.find: Abdomen soft and non-tender. No hepatosplenomegaly.

amsa-204.key: Jenny has a low-grade fever (37.8 °C), is thin (50 kg, BMI 19.5, about 9% of her body weight lost) and is mildly pale. She has blood-streaked mucopurulent sputum, reduced expansion at the right apex and coarse crackles in the right upper zone. In a woman born in Cambodia who visits every year, these findings point to upper lobe disease and probable pulmonary tuberculosis. Her heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure and SpO2 are normal, she has no clubbing, no enlarged lymph nodes, normal calves and no signs of spread outside the lungs. These findings make cancer and PE less likely and mean she is stable enough to manage as an outpatient. She still needs a mask and a separate room now, sputum for AFB and an urgent referral to the TB service.

amsa-212.vitals: Temperature 37.9 °C, HR 102 bpm regular, BP 128/78 mmHg, RR 18 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air, capillary BGL 5.6 mmol/L, pain 7/10, weight 78 kg (10:20)
amsa-212.general: Looks unwell and flushed. He lies still on the couch and winces when he shifts or coughs, so he moves carefully. Alert and cooperative, but worried. He breathes shallowly to avoid moving his abdomen.

steps.do: Look at the mucous membranes and test capillary refill
steps.find: Mucous membranes slightly dry. CRT 2 seconds.

steps.find: No clubbing, pallor or jaundice. No mouth ulcers.

steps.find: Chest clear with no wheeze. Heart sounds dual with no murmurs.

steps.find: Not distended and no scars. Shallow breathing to splint the abdomen. Coughing causes pain in the right iliac fossa.

steps.find: Percussion tenderness and rebound tenderness in the right iliac fossa.

steps.do: Test Rovsing's sign, the psoas sign (hip extension) and the obturator sign (internal rotation of the flexed hip)
steps.find: Rovsing's sign positive: pressing the left iliac fossa causes pain in the right iliac fossa. Psoas and obturator signs negative.

steps.do: Auscultate the abdomen
steps.find: Bowel sounds present, slightly reduced.

steps.find: Renal angles non-tender. Hernial orifices clear.

amsa-212.key: He has a low-grade temperature (37.9 °C) and a tachycardia (102 bpm). His tenderness is localised to McBurney's point with guarding, percussion and rebound tenderness, pain on coughing and a positive Rovsing's sign, which is localised peritonism in the right iliac fossa. Together with his history of periumbilical pain, anorexia and vomiting, this points strongly to acute appendicitis. Findings that argue against the alternatives: Murphy's sign is negative, the renal angles are non-tender, the hernial orifices and testes are normal, the abdomen is not distended and there are no mouth ulcers or pallor, so cholecystitis, renal colic, a hernia, torsion, obstruction and Crohn's are less likely.

amsa-213.vitals: HR 88 bpm regular, BP 112/70 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 37.6 °C; weight 58 kg, height 168 cm, BMI 20.5 kg/m²
amsa-213.general: Slim young woman who is alert and comfortable at rest, sitting still without distress. Not jaundiced and not obviously pale from the end of the bed. No drips, aids or medications at the bedside. Mildly embarrassed when bowels are discussed.

steps.find: Mild finger clubbing. No koilonychia, leuconychia or palmar erythema. Capillary refill under 2 seconds. Warm and well perfused.

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae for pallor and the sclerae for icterus; look for red or inflamed eyes (uveitis, episcleritis)
steps.find: Mild conjunctival pallor. No scleral icterus. Eyes not red or injected.

steps.do: Inspect the oral mucosa, tongue and gums with a torch for aphthous ulcers, angular stomatitis and glossitis
steps.find: No aphthous ulcers. Tongue and gums normal; no angular stomatitis. Mucous membranes moist.

steps.do: Palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes, including Virchow's node
steps.find: No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.find: No rashes, erythema nodosum or pyoderma. Joints not swollen or tender, with full range of movement.

steps.find: Heart sounds dual, no murmurs. Chest clear with vesicular breath sounds bilaterally.

amsa-213.key: Right iliac fossa tenderness with no peritonism, plus perianal inflammation with skin tags and mild finger clubbing, points to inflammatory bowel disease, and to Crohn's disease more than ulcerative colitis. It makes acute appendicitis unlikely. The low-grade fever of 37.6 °C, conjunctival pallor and blood on the glove suggest active inflammation and blood loss, which may be causing anaemia. A negative urine β-hCG rules out ectopic pregnancy, and a negative dipstick makes a UTI unlikely as the cause of her right iliac fossa pain.

amsa-214.key: Gary is tachycardic (HR 109) with dry mucous membranes and ongoing vomiting, so he is volume depleted. He has marked epigastric tenderness with only voluntary guarding, which fits acute pancreatitis rather than a perforation. There is no rigidity or rebound, Murphy's sign is negative and there is no jaundice. The things that point away from a dangerous mimic are: no pulsatile mass, equal pulses and equal BP in both arms (against AAA), and a clear chest with no surgical emphysema (against Boerhaave syndrome). He has no tremor and no stigmata of chronic liver disease, but his last drink was at about 1 am, so he still needs thiamine and monitoring for alcohol withdrawal.

amsa-215.key: Gabby has a fever of 38.6 °C, a heart rate of 110 and chills, with right upper quadrant tenderness, guarding there and a positive Murphy's sign. This points to acute cholecystitis rather than biliary colic, which would settle within a few hours. She has no jaundice, peritonism, pain at the renal angles or chest signs, and her urine dipstick and ECG are normal. That makes cholangitis, a perforated ulcer, kidney or urinary causes, right lower lobe pneumonia and a heart cause less likely. She has a negative beta-hCG still to come (Part 2), and her dry mucous membranes mean she needs IV fluids.

amsa-216.key: She is stable, with no signs of heart failure, a pericardial rub, aortic dissection (equal BP in both arms) or chest wall pain, so the ECG and serial high-sensitivity troponin must still be used to exclude ACS. Mild epigastric tenderness fits reflux or peptic disease. She has no pallor, koilonychia, Virchow's node, abdominal mass or melaena. Her weighed loss of about 5 kg (about 6%) confirms significant unintentional weight loss, an alarm feature that, together with her dysphagia, means she needs an urgent gastroscopy.

amsa-217.key: He has lost weight (about 4 kg in 8 months, BMI 19.8) and has signs of nutritional deficiency: conjunctival and palmar pallor and angular cheilitis. Along with a mildly distended, tympanic but non-tender abdomen and pale stool on rectal examination, this suggests malabsorption rather than IBS. He has a scratched rash on both knees, which is an extensor site and should make you think of dermatitis herpetiformis and coeliac disease. There are no signs of hyperthyroidism, no mouth ulcers or perianal disease to suggest Crohn's, no lymph nodes and normal observations, which makes the dangerous differentials less likely.

amsa-218.key: Jaundice, palmar erythema, spider naevi and a palpable spleen point to chronic liver disease with portal hypertension. There is no ascites, flap or oedema yet. The palpable purpura on both legs does not blanch and is small-vessel vasculitis, which with this blood-borne virus risk suggests cryoglobulinaemia. The negative urine blood and protein are reassuring for the kidneys, and the bilirubin in the urine fits conjugated (hepatic) jaundice.

steps.find: Dry mucous membranes, capillary refill 3 seconds, cool peripheries.

steps.find: Jaundiced skin and scleral icterus. Scratch marks on her forearms and legs. No xanthelasma. No bruising.

steps.find: No clubbing, leuconychia, palmar erythema or Dupuytren's contracture. Normal.

steps.find: Obese, not distended. No scars, no caput medusae and no visible masses.

steps.find: Tender in the right upper quadrant and epigastrium, with voluntary guarding in the right upper quadrant. No rigidity or rebound tenderness. Murphy's sign negative. Liver edge not palpable below the costal margin. Gallbladder not palpable. Spleen not palpable. No masses.

steps.find: No shifting dullness (no ascites). Bowel sounds present and normal.

steps.find: Not tender on either side.

amsa-219.key: She has Charcot's triad (jaundice, right upper quadrant pain and a fever of 38.6 °C). She also has new disorientation (wrong day, slow responses), tachycardia, tachypnoea, a soft BP of 104/66 and signs of poor perfusion. Together these point to acute cholangitis with sepsis and early organ dysfunction (heading towards Reynolds' pentad). The negative Murphy's sign, impalpable gallbladder, bilirubin-positive and urobilinogen-negative urine, and absent stigmata of chronic liver disease fit obstruction of the common bile duct by her known gallstones, rather than cholecystitis or liver disease. She needs an ambulance to the ED now, not outpatient tests.

amsa-220.key: Sarah has a sustained, regular tachycardia at 150/min with mild breathlessness and light-headedness. Her BP is maintained, she is warm with a CRT under 2 seconds, GCS is 15, and she has no chest pain or signs of heart failure. So she is haemodynamically stable and needs a monitored bed, pads, IV access and a senior review now, not DC cardioversion. The fine tremor, warm palms, brisk reflexes and a diffuse, smooth, non-tender goitre without eye signs point to thyrotoxicosis, probably Graves' disease, as the trigger. The normal heart sounds, normal JVP, clear lungs and no oedema argue against structural heart disease or heart failure.

amsa-221.key: He has a fast, irregularly irregular pulse with variable volume, a varying S1 and a pulse deficit (apex 132 against radial about 118). In a man with 40 minutes of sudden palpitations, this strongly suggests new-onset atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. He is haemodynamically stable: BP is normal, he is well perfused and alert, and there are no signs of heart failure, hypoxia or fever, so emergency DC cardioversion is not needed. There is no murmur, thyroid sign or chest finding to suggest valve disease, thyrotoxicosis or infection as a cause. An early 12-lead ECG and cardiac monitoring are still essential to confirm the rhythm and look for ischaemia.

steps.do: Palpate cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes, including the left supraclavicular fossa (Virchow's node); assess JVP
steps.find: No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, including the left supraclavicular fossa. JVP not raised

steps.do: Assess pulse rate, rhythm and character, palpate the apex beat, auscultate all areas for murmurs (including aortic stenosis) and rub, check peripheral pulses and for oedema
steps.find: Pulse regular, normal character. Apex beat not displaced. Heart sounds dual, no murmurs (no ejection systolic murmur), no pericardial rub. Peripheral pulses present. No peripheral oedema

steps.do: Palpate the sternum, chest wall and ribs for tenderness; inspect for bruising or a dermatomal rash
steps.find: No chest wall or rib tenderness. No bruising, no rash

steps.do: Assess chest expansion, percuss and auscultate the lung fields
steps.find: Normal, symmetrical expansion. Resonant throughout. Vesicular breath sounds, no wheeze or crackles

steps.do: Palpate all regions including epigastrium and right upper quadrant, test Murphy's sign, feel for masses and organomegaly
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, including epigastrium and right upper quadrant. Murphy's sign negative. No masses, no hepatomegaly or splenomegaly

steps.do: Inspect and palpate both calves for swelling and tenderness
steps.find: Soft, non-tender, no swelling bilaterally

bedside.find: 8.4 mmol/L (2 hours after lunch)
The practice nurse says, "I'll record it now." The ECG is handed over by the examiner in Part 2

amsa-222.key: The examination is normal apart from central obesity (BMI 29.0, waist 104 cm), which is a risk factor for reflux and for Barrett's oesophagus. There is no pallor, supraclavicular node, epigastric mass or weight loss to suggest malignancy, and no murmur, heart failure signs, chest wall tenderness, pleural or calf findings, or right upper quadrant tenderness to point to a cardiac, respiratory, musculoskeletal or biliary cause. Because his pain is worse with exercise and he is a 54-year-old man with diabetes, a 12-lead ECG is still needed, and a normal examination does not rule out stable angina.

amsa-223.vitals: Triage: HR 112/min regular, BP 132/84 mmHg, RR 26/min, SpO2 93% on room air, Temp 37.6 °C, pain 10/10. Repeat a few minutes later: HR 116/min, BP 126/80 mmHg, RR 28/min, SpO2 92% on room air.
amsa-223.general: Anxious and distressed by pain, sitting upright. Shallow, rapid breathing, but speaking in full sentences. Winces on deep breaths and coughing. Not cyanosed, not pale, not sweaty. Well nourished (68 kg, BMI about 25). Nicotine staining on the right fingers. On a cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands, check capillary refill, look for clubbing and cyanosis
steps.find: Warm peripheries, capillary refill 2 seconds. No clubbing, no peripheral cyanosis. Nicotine staining on the right fingers.

steps.do: Feel both radial pulses for rate, rhythm and volume, and check for radio-femoral delay
steps.find: 112/min, regular, good volume. Radial pulses equal on both sides. No radio-femoral delay.

steps.do: Measure BP in both arms
steps.find: Right arm 132/84 mmHg, left arm 130/82 mmHg. No significant difference between the arms.

steps.do: Assess the JVP and check the trachea
steps.find: JVP not raised. Trachea central.

steps.do: Palpate the praecordium for heaves and auscultate all areas, listening for P2, murmurs and a pericardial rub
steps.find: No right ventricular heave. Dual heart sounds, normal P2, no murmurs, no pericardial rub.
