steps.do: Inspect the chest and back for rash, bruising or deformity, and palpate the chest wall for tenderness
steps.find: No rash on the chest or back. No bruising or deformity. Chest wall not tender to palpation.

steps.do: Assess chest expansion, percuss and auscultate the front and back of the chest
steps.find: Expansion equal but shallow because of pain. Resonant to percussion throughout. Vesicular breath sounds with equal air entry. No crackles, no wheeze, no pleural rub.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen, including for a pulsatile mass
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No pulsatile mass.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate both legs, feel along the deep veins, check for pitting oedema, measure calf circumference 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity, and check pedal pulses and knees
steps.find: Right calf swollen, red and warm, with pitting oedema to the mid-shin. Tender along the deep veins of the calf and in the popliteal fossa. Calf circumference right 40 cm, left 36 cm (4 cm difference). Left leg normal. No varicose veins. Pedal pulses present on both sides. Bony crepitus in both knees, no effusion.

bedside.find: 5.8 mmol/L
Regular narrow-complex rhythm at about 112 to 116/min
The nurse has recorded it. The tracing is handed over for interpretation in Part 2.
Sent to the lab. Results are given in Part 2.

amsa-223.key: Bertha is tachycardic, tachypnoeic and hypoxic on room air, and her breathing and oxygen levels are getting worse between the two sets of observations. Her BP is normal, so she is not in shock. The chest examination is normal: no pneumothorax, consolidation, effusion, rub or chest wall tenderness, and arm BPs are equal. That makes the main dangerous mimics less likely, though it does not rule them out. Her swollen, red, tender right calf (4 cm larger than the left) is clinical DVT. Together with the sudden pleuritic pain, this makes PE the most likely diagnosis and gives a high Wells score, so she should go straight to imaging and be escalated to a senior.

amsa-245.vitals: Temperature 36.8 °C, BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 84/min regular, RR 16/min, SpO2 99% on room air, capillary glucose 5.6 mmol/L, pain 10/10
amsa-245.general: Alert and oriented. Clearly uncomfortable, sitting very still with sunglasses on and asking for the lights to be dimmed. Speaks quietly and slowly. Anxious and a little tearful when talking about stress. Not pale or flushed. No rash.

steps.do: Checks for neck stiffness by gentle passive neck flexion, then Kernig's sign (and Brudzinski's sign if tested)
steps.find: No neck stiffness. Kernig's sign negative. Brudzinski's sign negative.

steps.do: Looks at both fundi with an ophthalmoscope in the dimmed room, checking for papilloedema
steps.find: Both optic discs pink with sharp margins and no swelling. Spontaneous venous pulsations present. No haemorrhages.

steps.do: Tests visual acuity, visual fields to confrontation, pupils (including swinging light test), checks for ptosis and miosis, tests eye movements and inspects the conjunctivae
steps.find: Visual acuity 6/6 in each eye. Visual fields full to confrontation. Pupils equal, round and reactive to light, with no relative afferent pupillary defect. No ptosis or miosis. Eye movements full, with no nystagmus or double vision. No conjunctival redness or tearing.

steps.do: Tests facial sensation and facial movement, palate, tongue and shoulder shrug; looks for rhinorrhoea
steps.find: Facial sensation and movement normal and symmetrical. Palate, tongue and shoulder shrug normal. No rhinorrhoea.

steps.do: Checks for pronator drift, then tone, power, reflexes and sensation (light touch and pinprick, including the hands) in all four limbs, and plantar responses
steps.find: No pronator drift. Tone, power (5/5), reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical in all four limbs, including both hands. Plantars flexor bilaterally.

steps.do: Finger-nose and heel-shin testing, normal gait, heel-to-toe walking and Romberg's test
steps.find: Finger-nose and heel-shin normal. Gait normal, including heel-to-toe walking. Romberg negative.

steps.do: Palpates the temporal arteries and scalp, presses over the sinuses, palpates the neck and shoulder muscles and checks neck movement
steps.find: Temporal arteries palpable, pulsatile and non-tender. No scalp tenderness. Sinuses non-tender. No tenderness of the neck or shoulder muscles. Neck movements full.

steps.do: Comments on appearance, behaviour, speech, mood and affect, and asks about thoughts of self-harm
steps.find: Appropriately dressed, cooperative and anxious. Speech normal but quiet. Mood 'stressed', with an anxious affect. No thoughts of self-harm.

bedside.find: 5.6 mmol/L (normal)
Negative (last menstrual period about 2 weeks ago, normal). Full result handed over in Part 2.

bedside.test: Repeat blood pressure after 10 minutes' rest
bedside.find: 124/76 mmHg, HR 80/min regular (handed over in Part 2)

amsa-245.key: The important findings are normal ones: she is afebrile and normotensive, has no meningism, her discs are sharp with spontaneous venous pulsations, and there is no focal neurological deficit. This makes subarachnoid haemorrhage, meningitis, raised intracranial pressure and a persisting stroke deficit unlikely. A normal examination after a fully resolved, gradually spreading aura supports migraine with aura. Her normal BP also means a triptan can be used.

amsa-246.vitals: RR 16/min, SpO2 97% on room air, BP 156/88 mmHg (right arm), HR 86 bpm regular, temperature 37.4 °C, CRT 2 seconds, alert (AVPU A), pain 6/10. Weight 82 kg.
amsa-246.general: He is alert and comfortable at rest, sitting up on the trolley and rubbing his right temple. He speaks in full sentences and is articulate, though a little frustrated and worried. Not pale, flushed or sweaty. No rash. Not in respiratory distress. Weight 82 kg.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate both superficial temporal arteries along their course and feel their pulses, then palpate the scalp. Check the sinuses, temporomandibular joints and teeth.
steps.find: The right superficial temporal artery is thickened, nodular and tender, and its pulse is barely palpable. The left temporal artery is soft with a normal pulse. The scalp is tender over the right temple and parietal area. No rash or vesicles. Sinuses not tender. Temporomandibular joints non-tender and teeth normal.

steps.do: Test acuity in each eye separately with his glasses on, using a Snellen chart, then retest with a pinhole. Recheck after he reports that the eye is getting worse.
steps.find: Right 6/18, no better with a pinhole. Left 6/6. Rechecked after he reports worsening: right 6/36, left 6/6.

steps.do: Inspect the pupils at rest, then check direct and consensual light reflexes and do the swinging light test.
steps.find: Pupils equal at rest. Swinging light test shows a right relative afferent pupillary defect.

steps.do: Test each eye separately with Ishihara plates, then test visual fields to confrontation one eye at a time.
steps.find: Colour vision is reduced in the right eye (misses several Ishihara plates) and normal on the left. Confrontation shows loss of the inferior field in the right eye. The left field is full.

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae and corneas, feel both globes gently through closed lids, then look at both optic discs and retinas with an ophthalmoscope.
steps.find: Both eyes are white and quiet, the corneas are clear, and neither eye is hard or tender. The right optic disc is pale and swollen, with a small flame haemorrhage at the disc margin. The left disc is normal, with no papilloedema.

steps.do: Test eye movements, look for ptosis, and test facial symmetry and power, hearing, palate and tongue.
steps.find: Eye movements full with no double vision. No ptosis. Face symmetrical. Hearing, palate and tongue normal.

steps.do: Check for neck stiffness and do Kernig's sign. Ask about photophobia and look for a rash.
steps.find: No neck stiffness. Kernig's sign negative. No photophobia. No rash.

steps.do: Test tone, power, reflexes, sensation and coordination in all four limbs, check the plantar responses and watch him walk.
steps.find: Tone, power, reflexes, sensation and coordination normal and symmetrical. Plantars flexor. Gait normal.

steps.do: Assess active and passive range of movement of both shoulders and hips, and palpate for tenderness and synovitis.
steps.find: Full active and passive range of movement, with no tenderness and no synovitis.

steps.do: Feel the radial and brachial pulses on both sides, measure BP in both arms, listen for carotid, subclavian and axillary bruits, and auscultate the heart.
steps.find: Pulse 86 and regular. BP right arm 156/88, left arm 152/86. Radial and brachial pulses equal. No carotid, subclavian or axillary bruits. Heart sounds dual with no murmur.

bedside.find: 6.0 mmol/L. Normal, and the baseline before high-dose corticosteroids.

bedside.test: Repeat visual acuity (after he reports worsening)
bedside.find: Right 6/36 (down from 6/18), left 6/6. Vision in the right eye is getting worse.

bedside.test: Bloods (ESR, CRP, FBC, UEC, LFTs, glucose) collected at cannulation
bedside.find: Sent. The nurse says results will be available in Part 2.

amsa-246.key: A thickened, tender, nodular right temporal artery with a barely palpable pulse, plus right scalp tenderness, in a 64-year-old with a new headache strongly suggests giant cell arteritis. Right optic nerve ischaemia (arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy) is shown by reduced acuity that does not improve with a pinhole and falls from 6/18 to 6/36, a right RAPD, an inferior field defect, reduced colour vision and a pale swollen disc. Every vital sign is in the white zone, but this is a sight-threatening emergency: start IV methylprednisolone now, without waiting for results, and get a senior doctor and urgent ophthalmology review. The normal neurological examination, absent meningism and quiet, soft eyes make SAH, meningitis, a mass lesion and angle-closure glaucoma unlikely.

amsa-247.vitals: RR 18/min, SpO2 98% on room air, BP 112/68 mmHg, HR 116/min regular, temperature 39.2 °C, CRT 2 seconds, pain 8/10, BGL 5.4 mmol/L, weight 60 kg
amsa-247.general: Flushed and unwell young woman lying still on the trolley with her eyes half closed because of photophobia. She winces when her head is moved. She is alert and answers clearly but sounds flat and miserable. Mucous membranes are dry. Monitoring is attached.

steps.do: Assess GCS by its components and her orientation
steps.find: GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6). Oriented to time, place and person, with no confusion.

steps.do: Inspect all of the skin for a petechial or purpuric rash, including the legs, trunk, palms, soles and conjunctivae, and do a blanching (glass) test on any spots
steps.find: No rash, no petechiae and no purpura anywhere, including the palms, soles and conjunctivae.

steps.do: Check mucous membranes, capillary refill and peripheral temperature
steps.find: Dry mucous membranes. CRT 2 seconds. Peripheries warm.

steps.do: Test passive neck flexion, Kernig's sign and Brudzinski's sign
steps.find: Neck stiffness: she resists passive neck flexion. Kernig's sign positive. Brudzinski's sign positive. Photophobic.

steps.do: Examine the pupils and look at the optic discs with an ophthalmoscope
steps.find: Pupils 4 mm, equal and reactive to light. Optic discs sharp, no papilloedema.

steps.do: Screen visual fields, eye movements, facial symmetry and hearing
steps.find: Visual fields full. Eye movements full, with no nystagmus or diplopia. Face symmetrical. Hearing to whisper normal.

steps.do: Assess tone, power, reflexes, sensation, pronator drift, plantars and coordination
steps.find: Tone, power (5/5), reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical. No pronator drift. Plantars flexor. Coordination normal. Gait not tested because she is too unwell to stand.

steps.area: Head, eyes, ears, face and throat
steps.do: Look for head injury, red eye, temporal artery and jaw joint tenderness, sinus tenderness, otoscopy and the throat
steps.find: No signs of head injury. Eyes white, corneas clear. Temporal arteries non-tender and pulsatile. Jaw joints non-tender. Sinuses non-tender. Tympanic membranes normal. Throat normal.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and chest
steps.find: HR 116 regular, heart sounds dual, no murmur. Chest clear.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the abdomen
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No scars.

bedside.find: 5.4 mmol/L (normal)
Negative

amsa-247.key: Fever of 39.2 °C, tachycardia and dry mucous membranes, with neck stiffness, photophobia and positive Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs, mean bacterial meningitis with sepsis until proven otherwise. She needs blood cultures and immediate dexamethasone with IV ceftriaxone, without waiting for CT or LP. Her GCS is 15, she has no focal signs and no papilloedema, so there is no contraindication to going straight to LP. She has no rash for now, but her skin must be checked again, because meningococcal disease is still possible in an unvaccinated patient.

amsa-248.vitals: Practice nurse, 10:40: T 38.4 °C, HR 104 beats/min regular, BP 138/82 mmHg, RR 18/min, SpO2 97% on room air, alert, pain 10/10, finger-prick glucose 13.8 mmol/L
amsa-248.general: Unwell-looking, flushed and sweaty, grimacing in pain. He holds the left knee slightly bent (about 20–30°), supported and still, and will not stand on it. Alert and oriented, and answers appropriately.

steps.do: Expose both knees and compare them with the patient lying back. Look for swelling, redness, wounds, scars and red streaks up the thigh.
steps.find: The whole knee is swollen and the normal hollows beside the patella are lost. The skin over the whole knee is red. There is a 3 mm scabbed puncture wound 2 cm below the lower pole of the patella, just medial to the patellar tendon, with 3 cm of redness around it. No pus, no visible foreign body, no red streaks up the thigh, no surgical scars.

steps.do: Ask about pain first. Compare temperature with the back of the hand against the right knee. Check for an effusion (patellar tap or bulge test), find where it is tender, and feel for a separate swelling in front of the patella or over the patellar tendon.
steps.find: Clearly hotter than the right knee. Large effusion with a positive patellar tap. Tender all around the joint, including both joint lines, not just over the front of the patella. No separate fluctuant swelling in front of the patella or over the patellar tendon.

steps.do: Ask him to move the knee himself first, then try passive movement very gently without forcing it. Do not test gait.
steps.find: Active movement is only about 10° from the slightly bent position he holds. Any passive movement beyond a few degrees in any direction causes severe pain, so do not force it. Gait cannot be tested because he cannot bear weight.

steps.area: Joints above and below (left hip and ankle)
steps.do: Gently rotate the left hip passively and examine the left ankle.
steps.find: Left hip has full, pain-free passive rotation. Left ankle is normal.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate and move the right knee to compare.
steps.find: Bony enlargement and crepitus. No effusion, not warm, non-tender, flexion to 120°. Consistent with osteoarthritis.

steps.area: Hands, ears, elbows and feet (other joints and crystal disease)
steps.do: Look at the hands, the helix of the ears and the elbows for tophi. Examine both first MTP joints and screen the other joints.
steps.find: Squaring at the base of both thumbs (OA). No tophi on the ears, elbows or hands. Both first MTP joints are normal. No other swollen or tender joints.

steps.area: Lymph nodes, skin, eyes and mouth
steps.do: Feel the inguinal nodes. Look for lymphangitis, rash or pustules, red eyes and mouth ulcers.
steps.find: One tender 1 cm left inguinal node. No rash or pustules. Eyes not red. No mouth ulcers.

steps.do: Feel the left calf. Check the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on both sides, test monofilament sensation and look for foot ulcers.
steps.find: Left calf soft and non-tender. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses present on both sides. Monofilament sensation intact. No foot ulcers.

steps.area: Cardiovascular, respiratory and abdomen (other source, endocarditis)
steps.do: Listen to the heart for murmurs and to the chest, and palpate the abdomen.
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmur. Chest clear. Abdomen soft and non-tender.

bedside.find: 13.8 mmol/L (hyperglycaemia)
Midstream sample collected by the practice nurse at 10:50. The examiner gives the result in Part 2.

amsa-248.key: He has fever and tachycardia, a hot, red left knee with a large true effusion, tenderness all around the joint and severe pain on any movement, and a puncture wound just below the patella. In a man with diabetes and OA, this is septic arthritis until proven otherwise, not bursitis, which would cause a superficial swelling in front of the patella with movement relatively preserved. Normal first MTPs and no tophi count against gout, and the tender left inguinal node shows local spread. BP, SpO2 and mental state are normal, so there is no sign of shock, and the hyperglycaemia needs to be flagged to the hospital.

amsa-249.vitals: RR 18 /min, SpO2 97% on room air, BP 146/90 mmHg, HR 96 bpm regular, temperature 37.4 °C, CRT 2 seconds, pain 8/10; weight 112 kg, height 178 cm (BMI 35 kg/m²)
amsa-249.general: Alert and orientated, sitting on the trolley holding his left hand up against his chest and guarding it. He winces whenever anyone comes near it and is in obvious pain, but does not look systemically unwell. He is centrally obese (BMI 35). There is no pallor, sweating or rigors.

steps.do: Inspect the left ring finger and hand, both palm and back, including the skin, the nails and the rest of the finger.
steps.find: The DIP joint is swollen, with red, shiny, tense skin over it. There is no skin break, puncture wound, splinter or foreign body anywhere on the hand. The rest of the finger is normal in size, with no swelling of the whole finger (no dactylitis). Nails are normal.

steps.do: Gently feel the temperature and tenderness of the DIP joint and check for fluctuance.
steps.find: The DIP joint is hot and exquisitely tender. He pulls away from light touch. There is no fluctuance.

steps.do: Assess active and then passive movement at the DIP, PIP and MCP joints.
steps.find: Active and passive DIP movement are markedly reduced by pain. The PIP and MCP joints have a full range of movement.

steps.do: Check the resting posture of the finger, feel along the flexor sheath on the palm side, and passively extend the finger at the PIP and MCP joints.
steps.find: The finger is not held flexed. Swelling is confined to the DIP joint. There is no tenderness along the flexor sheath and no pain along the palm side of the finger on passive extension. No signs of flexor sheath infection.

steps.do: Check sensation on both sides of the fingertip and capillary refill in the fingertip.
steps.find: Sensation is normal on both sides of the fingertip and capillary refill is under 2 seconds. Neurovascularly intact.

steps.do: Inspect the hand and forearm for cellulitis and lymphangitis, and feel for epitrochlear and axillary lymph nodes.
steps.find: No cellulitis of the hand and no red streaks up the forearm. No epitrochlear or axillary lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Screen the other finger joints, both wrists, elbows, knees and ankles, and both first MTP joints, for swelling, warmth and tenderness.
steps.find: All normal, with no swelling, warmth or tenderness. Both first MTP joints are normal now.

steps.do: Inspect the helix of both ears, the extensor surfaces of the elbows, the fingers and the toes.
steps.find: No tophi.

steps.do: Look for psoriatic plaques on the elbows, knees, scalp, natal cleft and umbilicus, and check all the nails for pitting and onycholysis.
steps.find: No psoriatic plaques. No nail pitting or onycholysis.

bedside.find: 6.1 mmol/L
Normal: no leucocytes, nitrites, blood, protein or glucose

bedside.test: Pain score after analgesia and ice (if ordered)
bedside.find: Improved to 7/10 by the end of Part 1, so pain is still poorly controlled

amsa-249.key: He has an acute monoarthritis of his dominant left ring finger DIP joint: red, shiny, hot and exquisitely tender. He is afebrile, has no skin break, no flexor sheath signs and no spreading infection, which makes gout (his second attack, after the big toe last year) most likely. Because a normal temperature does not exclude septic arthritis, he still needs a joint aspirate with Gram stain and culture. There are no tophi, no psoriasis or nail changes and no other joints involved, which argues against chronic tophaceous gout, psoriatic arthritis and a polyarthritis. His BMI of 35 is a gout risk factor.

amsa-250.vitals: BP 132/82 mmHg, HR 76 beats/min regular, RR 14/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C. Weight 87 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 32 kg/m², waist circumference 102 cm.
amsa-250.general: Comfortable at rest and talking easily. Overweight, mainly around the waist. She is stiff getting up from the chair and walks slowly with a slightly antalgic gait, without a walking aid. She does not look unwell, pale or wasted.

steps.do: Watch her rise from the chair without using her arms, then walk to the end of the room, turn and walk back.
steps.find: Stiff and slow getting up from the chair. Slow gait that is slightly antalgic on both sides. Turns steadily and does not need an aid.

steps.do: Look at the backs and palms of both hands, the nails and the skin. Look at the elbows for nodules and plaques, and check for tophi.
steps.find: Firm swellings at the DIP joints of both hands (Heberden's nodes) and at several PIP joints (Bouchard's nodes). Squaring of both thumb bases. No redness. No ulnar deviation, swan-neck or boutonnière deformity. No nail pitting or onycholysis and no psoriatic plaques. No rheumatoid nodules at the elbows and no tophi.

steps.do: Compare the temperature of the joints with the back of your hand, palpate the swellings, do an MCP squeeze test and a thumb base (first CMC) grind test on both sides.
steps.find: The swellings are hard and bony, not soft or boggy. No warmth. MCP squeeze test negative and the MCPs are not swollen. Both thumb bases (first CMC joints) are tender, with crepitus on the grind test.

steps.do: Ask her to make a fist and open the hand fully, then test grip and pinch. Ask her to undo a button and open a jar.
steps.find: Can make a full fist, with slightly reduced flexion at the DIP joints. Grip and pinch are weaker than expected. She is slow to undo a button and to open a jar.

steps.do: With her standing then lying, check alignment and look for quadriceps wasting. Feel for warmth, do a patellar tap and a bulge test, and feel for crepitus while moving the knee. Measure range and test the collateral and cruciate ligaments on both sides.
steps.find: Mild varus alignment on both sides, with mild quadriceps wasting. Bony enlargement at the joint margins. No warmth. No effusion (patellar tap and bulge sign negative). Coarse crepitus through movement on both sides. Flexion to 110° on both sides, painful at the end of range. Ligaments stable.

steps.do: With her lying, move both hips through flexion and internal and external rotation with the hip and knee at 90°. Palpate both greater trochanters.
steps.find: Internal rotation reduced on both sides (about 15°) and reproduces groin pain. Flexion slightly reduced. No tenderness over the greater trochanters.

steps.do: Look at spinal alignment, palpate the midline and the paraspinal muscles, and assess flexion, extension and lateral flexion.
steps.find: Normal alignment. Mild paraspinal tenderness on both sides. No midline bony tenderness. Flexion and extension reduced and uncomfortable.

steps.do: Straight leg raise on both sides, then test power, sensation (including dermatomes) and knee and ankle reflexes in both legs.
steps.find: Straight leg raise negative on both sides. Power, sensation and reflexes in both legs normal.

steps.do: Move both shoulders and palpate the shoulder girdle. Palpate both temporal arteries. Inspect the skin, mouth and eyes.
steps.find: Shoulders move fully, with no pain and no tenderness over the shoulder girdle. Temporal arteries are non-tender with normal pulses. No rash, no mouth ulcers, eyes normal.

bedside.find: Normal: no blood, protein, glucose, leucocytes or nitrites.
5.9 mmol/L, normal.

amsa-250.key: Her hand swellings are hard and bony nodes (Heberden's and Bouchard's) at the DIPs, PIPs and thumb bases. The joints are not warm, there is no synovitis and the MCP squeeze test is negative, so the pattern is nodal osteoarthritis, not rheumatoid arthritis. Knee crepitus with varus alignment and no effusion, and reduced internal rotation of both hips that reproduces groin pain, show osteoarthritis of the knees and hips. Her BMI of 32 is a risk factor she can change. Pain-free shoulders, normal temporal arteries, normal skin and nails, and a normal neurological examination of the legs make PMR, GCA, psoriatic arthritis and a serious spinal cause unlikely.

amsa-251.vitals: RR 16, SpO2 99% on room air, BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 76 bpm regular, temperature 36.8 °C, CRT 2 seconds, pain 2/10 (dull mid-back ache and band around the waist), weight 65 kg
amsa-251.general: Lying comfortably on the trolley, alert and appears well. Frightened but not distressed. No walking aids. A urinary catheter is in place, draining clear urine. No tremor, chorea, myoclonus or other abnormal movements.

steps.do: Expose both legs with dignity, lying supine. Inspect for wasting, fasciculations, deformity, scars and skin changes, and tap the muscles to try to bring out fasciculations.
steps.find: No wasting, joint deformity, swelling, scars or skin changes. No fasciculations, including after tapping the muscles.

steps.do: Ask her to stand and walk, staying close to prevent a fall. Plan to test heel-to-toe, heels, toes, Romberg's test, squat and Trendelenburg.
steps.find: Unable to stand or walk. She says "I can't, my legs just won't hold me" and the nurse steps in to stop her falling. Heel-to-toe, heel and toe walking, Romberg's test, squat, Trendelenburg and the pull test cannot be done.

steps.do: Roll the legs, lift the knee quickly, and test for clonus at the ankle and knee (patella) on both sides.
steps.find: Increased, spastic tone in both legs, more on the right (a catch on quick knee flexion). No clonus at the ankles or knees.

steps.do: Test hip, knee and ankle movements on the MRC scale, comparing sides.
steps.find: Pyramidal pattern (flexors weaker than extensors), right worse. Right: hip flexion 3/5, extension 4/5, abduction 3/5, adduction 4/5; knee flexion 3/5, extension 4-/5; ankle dorsiflexion 2/5, plantarflexion 3/5, inversion and eversion 2/5. Left: hip flexion 4/5, extension 5/5, abduction 4/5, adduction 5/5; knee flexion 4/5, extension 4+/5; ankle dorsiflexion 3/5, plantarflexion 4/5, inversion and eversion 3/5.

steps.do: Test knee and ankle jerks (with reinforcement if needed) and plantar responses on both sides.
steps.find: Brisk knee and ankle jerks on both sides. Plantars upgoing (extensor) on both sides.

steps.do: Test heel-shin, toe-finger and foot tapping on both sides.
steps.find: Slow but accurate on both sides, in keeping with the weakness. No ataxia beyond what the weakness explains.

steps.do: With her eyes closed, test pinprick, temperature, light touch, vibration (128 Hz fork) and proprioception by dermatome, comparing sides against the sternum, then keep going up the trunk to find a level.
steps.find: Mostly dorsal column loss: proprioception absent at both great toes and ankles; vibration absent at the toes and ankles and reduced at the knees on both sides. Pinprick, temperature and light touch reduced (not absent) in all lower limb dermatomes and up the trunk to the umbilicus, more on the left, and normal above it. Sensory level at T10.

steps.do: With a chaperone and consent, test perianal sensation, then do a PR for resting tone and voluntary squeeze.
steps.find: Reduced perianal sensation, with tingling. Normal resting anal tone but reduced voluntary anal squeeze.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the spine for deformity, a step or tenderness. Palpate the abdomen and bladder.
steps.find: Spine: no deformity, no step and no tenderness. Abdomen soft and non-tender. Bladder not palpable with the catheter in.

steps.area: Upper limbs and cranial nerves (to complete)
steps.do: Complete with an upper limb neurological examination and cranial nerves, including visual acuity, pupils, eye movements and fundoscopy.
steps.find: Upper limbs: tone, power (5/5), reflexes, coordination and sensation normal and symmetrical. Cranial nerves: visual acuity 6/6 in each eye, no RAPD, eye movements full with no nystagmus, other cranial nerves normal. Fundoscopy: mild temporal pallor of the right optic disc; left disc normal.

bedside.find: 5.4 mmol/L
Negative
Drained 950 mL of clear urine, which confirms urinary retention

amsa-251.key: Spastic tone, brisk reflexes, upgoing plantars and pyramidal weakness (right worse), with no wasting or fasciculations, are upper motor neuron signs. With a T10 sensory level, sphincter involvement and normal arms and cranial nerves, this places the lesion in the thoracic spinal cord, not the cauda equina. A new paraparesis with a sensory level and urinary retention is cord compression until proven otherwise, so it needs senior review and an urgent MRI of the whole spine now. The patchy, partial, mostly dorsal column loss and the pale right optic disc (pointing to a past optic neuritis) suggest a demyelinating myelitis.

amsa-256.vitals: 10:05: Temp 36.8 °C, HR 92 bpm regular, BP 128/80 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, pain 4/10 at rest. Weight 72 kg.
amsa-256.general: Well and alert, and talks in full sentences. He is uncomfortable sitting, sits gingerly and shifts his weight to one side. He is not pale, jaundiced or distressed, and looks well hydrated.

steps.do: Does hand hygiene, introduces self, explains the examination in plain words, gains consent and offers a chaperone for any intimate part
steps.find: Peter agrees to the general and abdominal examination. He is a little embarrassed but settles with reassurance.

steps.do: Inspects the hands and nails for clubbing, pallor of the palmar creases and stigmata of chronic disease
steps.find: No clubbing, no palmar pallor and no leukonychia. Hands are warm and well perfused, with capillary refill under 2 seconds.

steps.do: Inspects the conjunctivae for pallor and the eyes for redness, and the mouth for ulcers and angular stomatitis
steps.find: No conjunctival pallor, no scleral icterus and no red eyes. No mouth ulcers, no angular stomatitis and no glossitis.

steps.do: Positions him supine, exposes the abdomen and inspects for scars, distension and masses
steps.find: Healed appendicectomy scar in the right iliac fossa. Abdomen is not distended and has no visible masses.

steps.do: Palpates lightly and then deeply in all regions, feels for the liver and spleen, and feels for faecal loading in the left iliac fossa
steps.find: Soft and non-tender throughout. No masses, no palpable faecal loading and no hepatosplenomegaly.

steps.do: Percusses the abdomen and listens for bowel sounds
steps.find: Resonant, with no shifting dullness. Bowel sounds are normal.

steps.do: Palpates both inguinal regions for lymphadenopathy
steps.find: Inguinal lymph nodes are not enlarged on either side.

steps.area: Perianal examination and digital rectal examination
steps.do: Explains the examination in plain words, gains explicit consent and offers a chaperone. Describes the position: left lateral with knees drawn up, undressed from the waist down with a sheet for cover. States they will inspect the perianal skin and natal cleft first, part the buttocks gently, and not force a rectal examination if it is too painful
steps.find: Peter agrees and the practice nurse is present as a chaperone. The findings of the perianal examination will be given to you in Part 2. (If consent is not sought or a chaperone is not offered, Peter says: "Hang on, what are you going to do?")

bedside.find: 4/10 at rest, a dull ache about 3 hours after this morning's bowel motion.
72 kg.
Not indicated for this presentation. If done, it is normal: no blood, protein, leucocytes, nitrites or glucose.

bedside.test: Perianal inspection, digital rectal examination and proctoscopy
bedside.find: Results are given in Part 2.

amsa-256.key: Peter is afebrile with a normal blood pressure. His heart rate of 92 fits the pain from this morning's bowel motion, so he is systemically well, which argues against a perianal abscess or cellulitis. A soft, non-tender abdomen with no masses or faecal loading, no pallor, no mouth ulcers and no lymphadenopathy points to a local anal cause rather than inflammatory bowel disease or cancer. The key step in Part 1 is gaining explicit consent for a chaperoned perianal examination in the left lateral position, inspecting gently first and not forcing a rectal examination.

amsa-257.vitals: 10:20, seated at rest on room air: HR 68 beats/min, regular; BP 122/74 mmHg; RR 14 breaths/min; SpO2 99% on room air; temperature 36.8 °C.
amsa-257.general: Tall, slim young man sitting comfortably with his shirt off. He is pink, not distressed and speaks in full sentences. He has no inhaler, spacer or oxygen with him. Height 186 cm, weight 72 kg (BMI 20.8).

steps.do: Inspect for peripheral cyanosis, clubbing and tar staining. Check for wasting of the small muscles and test finger abduction strength. Check for wrist tenderness, asterixis and a fine tremor.
steps.find: Warm and pink. No peripheral cyanosis, clubbing or tar staining. No wasting of the small muscles, and finger abduction strength is normal. No wrist tenderness. No asterixis or fine tremor.

steps.do: Press over the frontal and maxillary sinuses. Look at the eyes for pallor, icterus and Horner's syndrome. Look in the nose at the turbinates, septum and for polyps. Use a torch and tongue depressor to look at the pharynx, mouth and tongue.
steps.find: No sinus tenderness. No conjunctival pallor or scleral icterus, and no ptosis or miosis. The turbinates are not engorged, the septum is midline and there are no polyps. The pharynx is not crowded, there are no ulcers, the tonsils are not enlarged and there is no central cyanosis.

steps.do: Feel all cervical node groups, including the supraclavicular nodes. Check tracheal position and look for a tracheal tug. Test Pemberton's sign. Look at the JVP.
steps.find: No cervical or supraclavicular lymph nodes. Trachea midline, with no tracheal tug. Pemberton's sign negative. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Inspect the front and back for scars, rashes, swelling, symmetry and chest wall deformity. Watch the lower ribs for Hoover's sign.
steps.find: No scars, rashes or swelling. The chest is symmetrical, with no pectus excavatum or carinatum, barrel chest, Harrison's sulcus, kyphosis or scoliosis. Hoover's sign absent.

steps.do: Feel for rib tenderness and subcutaneous emphysema. Locate the apex beat. Measure chest expansion and compare the two sides.
steps.find: No rib tenderness and no subcutaneous emphysema. Apex beat in the 5th intercostal space in the midclavicular line. Chest expansion is 6 cm and symmetrical.

steps.do: Percuss from the clavicles (including the apices) downwards, anteriorly, laterally and posteriorly, with his arms crossed for the back. Compare left with right.
steps.find: Resonant throughout and equal on both sides, front, sides and back, including the apices.

steps.do: Listen anteriorly, laterally and posteriorly while he breathes through his mouth, comparing sides. Test vocal resonance.
steps.find: Normal vesicular breath sounds throughout, with no added sounds (no wheeze, crackles or pleural rub). Vocal resonance normal and symmetrical.

steps.do: Feel the pulse and listen to the heart, lying and on standing.
steps.find: Pulse regular. Heart sounds dual, with no murmurs, including on standing.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the calves for swelling, oedema and tenderness, and compare their size.
steps.find: No swelling, oedema or calf tenderness. The calves are equal in size.

bedside.find: Not present. Systolic pressure falls by less than 10 mmHg on inspiration.
These will be given to you in Part 2.
Not done yet. A resting 12-lead ECG can be done in the practice today (this is discussed in Part 2).

amsa-257.key: Every finding is normal: observations, aids, hands, face, neck, chest and legs. The trachea is midline, expansion is symmetrical (6 cm), percussion is resonant everywhere including the apices, and breath sounds are vesicular with no wheeze. This makes a pneumothorax in this tall, slim young man very unlikely, and there is no sign of current airway obstruction. With HR under 100, SpO2 99% and no signs of DVT, PE is unlikely (he meets these PERC criteria), and the regular pulse with no murmur is reassuring for a cardiac cause. The findings fit physiological breathlessness after an unaccustomed run. A normal examination at rest does not exclude exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.

amsa-258.vitals: Temperature 36.7 °C, HR 76 beats/min regular, BP 116/72 mmHg, RR 14/min, SpO2 99% on room air, weight 64 kg, height 166 cm (BMI 23.2 kg/m²).
amsa-258.general: Well and comfortable at rest, normal build. Rubs her hands from time to time. No Cushingoid features. No walking aids, splints or oxygen.

steps.do: Inspect the face, scalp, mouth and eyes. Check the scalp, behind the ears, the umbilicus and the natal cleft for psoriasis.
steps.find: No malar rash, alopecia or mouth ulcers. Eyes are not red, with no scleritis or episcleritis. No psoriatic plaques on the scalp, behind the ears, at the umbilicus or in the natal cleft.

steps.do: With both hands resting on a pillow and the arms exposed above the elbows, rings and watch removed, inspect the backs of both hands, the wrists and the nails.
steps.find: Both sides are swollen in the same places: both wrists, the 2nd and 3rd MCP joints of both hands, and the 2nd, 3rd and 4th PIP joints of both hands. The swelling at the PIPs is spindle-shaped (fusiform). No redness. The DIP joints look normal. Fingers are straight: no ulnar deviation, swan neck, boutonnière or Z-thumb. No nodules, scars or muscle wasting. Nails normal: no pitting, ridging, onycholysis or nail-fold lesions. No Heberden's or Bouchard's nodes, no squaring at the base of the thumb, no tophi, no dactylitis.

steps.do: Turn the hands over and inspect the palms.
steps.find: No thenar or hypothenar wasting, no palmar erythema, no scars.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate both elbows and the extensor surfaces of the forearms.
steps.find: No nodules, plaques or tophi. No swelling, warmth or tenderness.

steps.area: Palpation of the wrists and hands
steps.do: Ask about pain first and watch her face. Compare the temperature of the wrists with the forearms using the back of the hand. Palpate the wrists in slight flexion and the ulnar styloids. Feel the MCPs with both thumbs, feel the PIPs and DIPs between two hands, then do the MCP squeeze test.
steps.find: Both wrists feel slightly warmer than the forearms. Both wrists are tender along the joint line, with soft, boggy, spongy swelling over the back of the wrist. Both ulnar styloids are tender. The 2nd and 3rd MCPs and the 2nd, 3rd and 4th PIPs of both hands are tender, with soft, spongy swelling (not hard or bony). The DIP joints are not tender or swollen. Squeezing across the MCPs hurts in both hands.

steps.do: Prayer and reverse prayer signs, active wrist flexion and extension, then ask her to make a fist. Passively move the finger joints.
steps.find: She cannot press her palms flat together with the wrists bent back, and the backs of her hands do not fully meet in reverse prayer. Wrist flexion and extension are reduced to about 50° each way and painful at the end of range. Her fist is incomplete, with the fingertips 1 cm short of the palm on both sides. The finger joints otherwise move through their range, with no deformities to correct.

steps.do: Tinel's and Phalen's tests on both sides. Test light touch in the median, ulnar and radial nerve areas.
steps.find: Tinel's and Phalen's tests are negative on both sides. Sensation is normal in the median, ulnar and radial areas.

steps.do: Test thumb opposition, power grip and key grip. Ask her to do up a button and write a sentence.
steps.find: Thumb opposition is intact. Grip is weak on both sides because of pain. Key grip is painful but present. She does up a button slowly and writes slowly but legibly.

steps.do: Inspect both feet, toes and nails, and squeeze across the MTP joints.
steps.find: Squeezing across the MTPs is tender on both sides. No visible swelling, no MTP crowding or deformity, no tophi, no dactylitis, no psoriasis and no nail changes.

steps.area: Other joints, entheses and systemic features
steps.do: Screen the shoulders, knees and ankles. Palpate the Achilles tendons and plantar fascia insertions. Do Schober's test. Auscultate the heart and lungs, palpate the spleen and check for lymph nodes.
steps.find: Shoulders, knees and ankles are not swollen or tender. Achilles and plantar fascia insertions are not tender. Schober's test is normal. Dual heart sounds, no murmur, no pericardial rub. Chest clear, no fine crackles. Spleen not palpable. No lymphadenopathy.

bedside.find: Normal: no blood, no protein, no leucocytes or nitrites.
64 kg, 166 cm, BMI 23.2 kg/m².

amsa-258.key: Ms Little has symmetrical, warm, soft, boggy swelling of both wrists, the 2nd and 3rd MCPs and the 2nd to 4th PIPs. She also has a positive MCP squeeze test, tender ulnar styloids and tender MTP squeeze in both feet, and her DIPs are spared. This is active synovitis in the typical pattern of rheumatoid arthritis. The swelling is soft, not bony, and there are no Heberden's or Bouchard's nodes, nail changes, dactylitis, psoriasis, tophi or lupus features, which argues against osteoarthritis, psoriatic arthritis, gout and SLE. She has no deformities or nodules yet, and her carpal tunnel tests are negative, so this is early disease and there is still time to protect her joints by treating it promptly.

amsa-263.vitals: BP 124/81 mmHg, HR 71 bpm regular, RR 12 breaths/min, Temp 37.4 °C, SpO2 98% on room air
amsa-263.general: Well, alert young man sitting comfortably and in no distress. Normal build (weight 74 kg, height 180 cm, BMI 23). Not visibly jaundiced in the skin. Not oedematous. Lying comfortably at 0 degrees with the abdomen exposed. Fully oriented and talking normally.

steps.do: Inspects the nails and palms for clubbing, leukonychia, palmar erythema and Dupuytren's contracture. Asks him to hold his arms out with wrists extended for 15 seconds to look for a flap.
steps.find: No clubbing, leukonychia, palmar erythema or Dupuytren's contracture. No asterixis (flap).

steps.do: Inspects the forearms and upper arms for bruising, petechiae, scratch marks, injection marks and muscle wasting.
steps.find: No bruising, petechiae, scratch marks or injection marks. No muscle wasting.

steps.do: In natural light, asks him to look down while gently lifting the upper lids to inspect the sclerae. Pulls down the lower lids to check the conjunctivae for pallor. Inspects the lips, tongue and mouth.
steps.find: Mild scleral icterus. No conjunctival pallor. Mouth normal: no ulcers, normal tongue, no angular stomatitis, no fetor hepaticus.

steps.do: Palpates the cervical, supraclavicular and axillary lymph nodes. Inspects the chest and back for spider naevi and the chest for gynaecomastia.
steps.find: No cervical, supraclavicular or axillary lymphadenopathy. No spider naevi. No gynaecomastia.

steps.do: Inspects the abdomen from the end of the bed and from the side, and asks him to cough, looking for distension, scars, masses, visible pulsation, distended veins and hernias.
steps.find: Abdomen flat, not distended. No scars, masses, visible pulsation, spider naevi or caput medusae. No hernias on coughing.

steps.do: Palpates all 9 regions, light then deep, watching his face. Palpates for the liver and spleen starting in the right iliac fossa, ballots both kidneys and palpates the aorta.
steps.find: Soft and non-tender with no guarding in all 9 regions on light and deep palpation. Liver edge not palpable. Spleen and kidneys not palpable. Aorta normal, not expansile.

steps.do: Percusses the upper and lower borders of the liver in the mid-clavicular line, percusses over the spleen, and percusses the flanks for shifting dullness.
steps.find: Liver span about 10 cm (normal). No splenic dullness. Resonant flanks with no shifting dullness (no ascites).

steps.do: Listens for bowel sounds and for renal and aortic bruits.
steps.find: Normal bowel sounds. No renal or aortic bruits. No hepatic bruit or rub.

steps.do: Tests Murphy's sign in the right upper quadrant, checks McBurney's point and Rovsing's sign, and looks for peritonism (guarding, rebound, percussion tenderness).
steps.find: Murphy's sign negative. No tenderness at McBurney's point; Rovsing's sign negative. No guarding, rebound or percussion tenderness.

steps.do: Checks the ankles and shins for pitting oedema. Thanks him, offers help to dress, and says they would complete the exam with external genitalia and a PR only if indicated.
steps.find: No pitting oedema of the legs.

bedside.find: Dark amber urine. Bilirubin positive (++). Urobilinogen normal. Blood, protein, leucocytes, nitrites and ketones negative. Specific gravity 1.020.
5.4 mmol/L (normal, no hypoglycaemia)
74 kg, 180 cm, BMI 23 kg/m²

amsa-263.key: Josh is a well young man. The only signs are mild scleral icterus and a temperature of 37.4 °C, and urine dipstick shows bilirubin, which means conjugated bilirubin and points away from a pre-hepatic cause. He has no peripheral signs of chronic liver disease, no hepatosplenomegaly and a negative Murphy's sign, which fits an acute hepatic process such as viral hepatitis rather than chronic liver disease or biliary obstruction. With no asterixis, a normal mental state, no bruising and a normal glucose, there are no signs of acute liver failure, so he can be worked up in general practice.

amsa-265.vitals: HR 84 regular, BP 132/80 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C. Weight 68 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 25 kg/m2, the same weight as in her records from a year ago.
amsa-265.general: Well and comfortable at rest. Looks a little pale. Not jaundiced. Not cachectic. Chatty and calm, but anxious underneath.

steps.do: Inspect the palms, palmar creases and nails; look for koilonychia and clubbing
steps.find: Palms and palmar creases are a normal colour. No koilonychia and no clubbing. Nicotine staining on the right index and middle fingers.

steps.do: Look for conjunctival pallor and scleral icterus; inspect the mouth for angular stomatitis and ulcers
steps.find: Mild conjunctival pallor. No scleral icterus. No angular stomatitis or mouth ulcers.

steps.do: Palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes (including Virchow's node) and the thyroid
steps.find: No cervical or supraclavicular lymph nodes. Thyroid not enlarged.

steps.do: Auscultate the chest and the heart
steps.find: Chest clear. Heart sounds dual with no murmurs.

steps.do: Inspect the abdomen with the patient lying flat, looking for distension, scars and visible masses
steps.find: Not distended. No scars. No visible masses.

steps.do: Palpate all nine regions lightly then deeply, including both iliac fossae; feel for the liver and spleen; percuss and test for shifting dullness
steps.find: Soft and non-tender in all regions. No masses, including in the left and right iliac fossae. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly. Percussion note normal throughout; no shifting dullness.

steps.do: Listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: Bowel sounds present and normal.

steps.do: Palpate both inguinal regions
steps.find: Inguinal nodes not enlarged.

steps.do: Explain, gain consent and have a chaperone; inspect the perianal area at rest and on straining; do a digital rectal examination; offer proctoscopy
steps.find: Perianal skin normal apart from healed scars from the 2018 haemorrhoidectomy. No external haemorrhoids, fissure, skin tags or prolapse, including on straining. Normal anal tone. No mass within reach of the finger, and the rectal wall feels smooth. Soft brown stool on the glove with streaks of dark red blood mixed through it. No melaena. Proctoscopy: no internal haemorrhoids or bleeding point in the anal canal.

steps.do: Test power, reflexes and sensation in both legs, including the saddle area
steps.find: Normal power, reflexes and sensation in both legs, including around the saddle area.

bedside.find: No blood, protein, leucocytes or nitrites. No haematuria.
5.6 mmol/L, normal.

bedside.test: Blood tests (FBC, iron studies, UEC, LFTs, calcium, TSH)
bedside.find: Taken today. Results will be available in Part 2.

amsa-265.key: The important findings are mild conjunctival pallor and dark red blood mixed through the stool on rectal examination. There are no haemorrhoids, fissure or anal bleeding point to explain the blood, which points to a source higher in the colon. The normal abdomen, absence of a rectal mass, stable weight and normal observations do not exclude colorectal cancer, because most of the colon is out of reach of the finger. These findings support urgent colonoscopy, not an FOBT.

amsa-266.vitals: HR 56/min regular, BP 128/86 mmHg sitting and 126/84 mmHg standing (no postural drop), RR 14/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 36.1 °C, weight 72 kg (68 kg three months ago), height 165 cm, BMI 26.4 kg/m²
amsa-266.general: Looks tired but alert, and a little slow to respond. Mild puffiness around the eyes. Her voice is normal and not hoarse. Her affect is slightly flat but reactive. She is comfortable at rest and not short of breath.

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands for temperature and skin texture, look for a fine tremor with the arms outstretched, check the palmar creases for pigmentation, and do Tinel and Phalen tests for carpal tunnel syndrome.
steps.find: Hands are cool and dry. No tremor. Palmar creases are not pigmented. Tinel and Phalen tests are negative.

steps.do: Feel the radial pulse for rate and rhythm.
steps.find: 56/min and regular (bradycardic).

steps.do: Inspect the face and eyebrows, look at the conjunctivae for pallor and the sclerae for jaundice, and inspect the buccal mucosa and tongue.
steps.find: Mild periorbital puffiness. The outer third of the eyebrows is thinned. Conjunctivae are pale. No jaundice. Buccal mucosa is not pigmented and the tongue is normal (no glossitis).

steps.do: Inspect and feel the skin of the arms and shins, and inspect the scalp hair.
steps.find: Dry, coarse skin on the arms and shins. Diffuse thinning of the scalp hair.

steps.do: Inspect from the front with the neck slightly extended, with a sip of water and with tongue protrusion. Palpate from behind for size, consistency, tenderness and nodules, and for the lower border. Check the trachea, cervical lymph nodes and Pemberton's sign, and auscultate for a bruit.
steps.find: Small diffuse goitre, visible with the neck extended. It rises on swallowing but not on tongue protrusion. Firm, rubbery, smooth and non-tender, with no discrete nodule. The lower border is palpable. Trachea central. Pemberton's sign negative. No cervical lymphadenopathy. No bruit.

steps.do: Assess the JVP, auscultate the heart and check for peripheral oedema.
steps.find: JVP not raised. Heart sounds dual with no murmur or rub. No peripheral oedema.

steps.do: Auscultate the chest.
steps.find: Chest clear, with good air entry on both sides.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen for tenderness, organomegaly and masses.
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No hepatosplenomegaly or masses.

steps.do: Test power in all limbs, ask her to rise from a chair without using her arms, and test the knee and ankle reflexes, watching the relaxation phase.
steps.find: Power 5/5 throughout, and she rises from the chair without using her arms. Knee reflexes are normal. Both ankle jerks are present with a slow relaxation phase.

steps.do: Test vibration and joint position sense at both great toes, and do Romberg's test (screening for B12 deficiency).
steps.find: Vibration and joint position sense are normal at both great toes. Romberg's test is negative.

bedside.find: 7.2 mmol/L
128/86 mmHg sitting, 126/84 mmHg standing, with no postural drop and no symptoms
72 kg (up 4 kg from 68 kg three months ago), 165 cm, BMI 26.4 kg/m²
Sinus bradycardia at 56/min with normal axis and intervals. No ischaemic changes.
No glucose, ketones, protein, blood, leucocytes or nitrites

amsa-266.key: Jenny has gained 4 kg and has bradycardia, cool dry skin, thinning hair and outer eyebrows, periorbital puffiness, slow-relaxing ankle jerks and a small, diffuse, firm, rubbery, non-tender goitre with no nodule. This picture strongly suggests autoimmune (Hashimoto) primary hypothyroidism in a woman with type 1 diabetes. Her pale conjunctivae point to anaemia. Her normal tongue, sensation and Romberg's test make severe B12 deficiency less likely but do not rule it out. There is no pigmentation and no postural drop, which argues against Addison disease before she starts thyroxine.

amsa-268.vitals: RR 18/min, SpO2 98% on room air, HR 94/min regular, BP 138/86 mmHg, temperature 36.8 °C, alert (AVPU A), pain 10/10. These were taken by the practice nurse at 09:05 during the attack; the full chart is handed over in Part 2.
amsa-268.general: Abdul is in severe pain and cannot sit still. He rocks in the chair, holds the left side of his head and paces if allowed. He is alert and fully oriented, and speaks in short answers because of the pain. He looks well apart from the pain. No rash. Towards the end of Part 1 the pain starts to ease and he can sit a little more still.

steps.area: Eyes and face (inspected during the attack)
steps.do: Inspect both eyes, eyelids and nostrils, comparing left with right
steps.find: Left conjunctiva red, with tears running from the left eye. Clear discharge from the left nostril. Mild drooping of the left upper eyelid. Right eye and nostril normal. No eyelid swelling or facial sweating.

steps.do: Compare pupil size, then test the direct and consensual light reflexes and do the swinging light test
steps.find: Left pupil 2 mm, right 4 mm. Both react to light directly and consensually. No relative afferent pupillary defect. With the mild left ptosis, this is a partial left Horner's syndrome during the attack.

steps.do: Look at both optic discs with an ophthalmoscope
steps.find: Optic discs pink with sharp margins on both sides. No papilloedema. Venous pulsations present.

steps.do: Test visual acuity, confrontation visual fields, eye movements, facial sensation in V1 to V3, the corneal reflex, facial movements and the lower cranial nerves
steps.find: Visual acuity 6/6 in each eye. Visual fields full. Eye movements full, with no double vision or nystagmus. Facial sensation normal in V1, V2 and V3 on both sides. Corneal reflex present. Facial movements symmetrical. Other cranial nerves normal.

steps.do: Check for pronator drift, then test tone, power, reflexes, plantar responses, sensation and coordination
steps.find: No pronator drift. Tone, power, reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical. Plantars flexor. Finger-nose and heel-shin testing normal.

steps.do: Watch his normal walk and heel-to-toe walking
steps.find: Normal gait. Heel-to-toe walking normal.

steps.do: Check for neck stiffness and Kernig's sign, and inspect the skin for a rash
steps.find: No neck stiffness. Kernig's sign negative. No rash.

steps.do: Feel the temporal arteries, scalp, sinuses and temporomandibular joints, and test neck movement
steps.find: Temporal arteries pulsatile and not tender. No scalp tenderness. No tenderness over the sinuses. Temporomandibular joints normal. Full, pain-free neck movement.

bedside.find: 6/6 in the right eye and 6/6 in the left eye.
10/10 at 09:05 during the attack, easing towards the end of Part 1.
Arranged by the GP supervisor once the attack settles. The result is handed over in Part 2.
Requested by the GP supervisor and done 5 days later. The report is handed over in Part 2.

amsa-268.key: During the attack the left eye is red and watering, the left nostril is running, and he has a partial left Horner's syndrome (left pupil 2 mm against 4 mm on the right, with mild left ptosis). He is also restless. Together these are the same-sided autonomic features of cluster headache. The rest of the examination is normal: no papilloedema, no focal neurological signs, no meningism or fever, and normal temporal arteries. This argues against raised intracranial pressure, a space-occupying lesion, subarachnoid haemorrhage, meningitis and giant cell arteritis. An MRI is still needed to exclude a structural mimic, and if the Horner's persisted between attacks, carotid dissection would need to be excluded.

amsa-271.vitals: HR 74 regular, BP 128/80 mmHg, RR 14/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C, weight 82 kg, height 178 cm, BMI 26 kg/m2 (overweight range)
amsa-271.general: Well, comfortable man sitting at rest. A little embarrassed and visibly worried, but not in distress. Not pale, jaundiced or short of breath. Looks his stated age. Overweight build with no obvious recent weight loss.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for koilonychia, clubbing, palmar pallor and palmar erythema
steps.find: Normal. No koilonychia, clubbing, palmar pallor or palmar erythema.

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae for pallor and the sclerae for icterus
steps.find: Conjunctivae pink. No scleral icterus.

steps.do: Inspect the abdomen for distension, scars and signs of chronic liver disease
steps.find: Not distended. No spider naevi or caput medusae.

steps.do: Palpate lightly and then deeply for tenderness and masses, feel for the liver and spleen, check for ascites and listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No masses. No hepatosplenomegaly. No ascites. Bowel sounds normal.

steps.do: Palpate the supraclavicular and inguinal lymph nodes
steps.find: No supraclavicular or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Explain why a perianal and rectal examination is needed and what it involves, gain specific consent, and have the practice nurse present as chaperone
steps.find: Peter understands and agrees. The practice nurse is present. He lies in the left lateral position with his knees drawn up.

steps.do: Inspect the perianal skin at rest, then ask him to bear down
steps.find: Normal perianal skin. No external haemorrhoids, skin tags, fissure, fistula opening or excoriation. Nothing prolapses when he bears down.

steps.do: Use a lubricated gloved finger to assess anal tone, tenderness, rectal wall masses and the prostate, then check the glove
steps.find: Normal anal tone, not tender. No masses felt. Prostate smooth and normal-sized. Soft brown stool on the glove, with no blood or melaena.

steps.do: Offer or recommend proctoscopy, because internal haemorrhoids usually cannot be felt on rectal examination
steps.find: Your supervising GP will do this at the end of the consultation. The report is given in Part 2.

bedside.find: Deferred. The supervising GP will do it at the end of the consultation, and the report is given in Part 2.
Requested. Results are given in Part 2.
Not appropriate. This is a screening test for people without symptoms, not a test for visible rectal bleeding.

amsa-271.key: His observations are normal and there are no signs of anaemia, no abdominal mass, no lymph node swelling and no signs of chronic liver disease. Nothing in the examination suggests chronic blood loss, cancer or portal hypertension. The perianal inspection is normal and nothing prolapses, which argues against a fissure, external haemorrhoids or prolapsing haemorrhoids. The rectal examination is also normal, but internal haemorrhoids usually cannot be felt and a normal DRE does not clear the bowel higher up, so he needs proctoscopy and, later, colonoscopy.

amsa-301.vitals: BP 148/90 mmHg (repeat 146/88 mmHg), HR 78/min regular, RR 14/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C, weight 102 kg, height 178 cm, BMI 32 kg/m², waist 112 cm
amsa-301.general: Comfortable at rest, alert and orientated. Central obesity. Well hydrated. No ketotic breath. No Cushingoid features. Sitting in shorts, happy to take off his boots and socks for the examination.

steps.do: With both legs exposed to the shorts, inspect from thigh to ankle and compare sides. Look for scars, hair loss, shiny atrophic skin, ulcers, varicose veins, venous skin changes and necrobiosis lipoidica.
steps.find: No scars. Hair is normal. No shiny atrophic skin, no arterial or venous ulcers, no varicose veins and no venous skin changes. No necrobiosis lipoidica. There is a soft swelling, about 4 cm across, on the left anterolateral thigh at his injection site.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the insulin injection sites on both thighs (and the abdomen if he uses it).
steps.find: The left anterolateral thigh swelling is soft, rubbery and non-tender, consistent with lipohypertrophy. The right thigh is normal.

steps.do: With shoes and socks off, inspect both feet including the soles, the heels and between every toe. Look for ulcers, fissures, callus, infection, nail disease and deformity.
steps.find: Dry skin on both feet. Callus under the right first metatarsal head. White, macerated, peeling skin between the 4th and 5th toes of the left foot (interdigital tinea). No ulcers, fissures, cellulitis or nail infection. Heels intact. No Charcot deformity or midfoot collapse.

steps.do: Compare the temperature of both feet with the back of the hand. Palpate the dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial and popliteal pulses on both sides. Check capillary refill at the great toes.
steps.find: Both feet are warm and the same temperature, and neither foot is hot or swollen. Dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial and popliteal pulses are palpable on both sides. Capillary refill is under 2 seconds.

steps.do: Demonstrate on the sternum first. With his eyes closed, apply the monofilament until it buckles at the plantar great toe and the 1st and 5th metatarsal heads of each foot.
steps.find: Not felt at the plantar great toe or the 1st and 5th metatarsal heads on either foot. This is loss of protective sensation on both sides.

steps.do: Test from distal to proximal on each leg to find the level where sensation changes, and compare sides.
steps.find: Light touch and pinprick are reduced up to the midfoot on both sides, in a symmetrical stocking distribution. Normal above that level.

steps.do: Use a 128 Hz tuning fork, starting at the great toe and moving up to the medial malleolus and then the knee. Test great toe joint position sense, then the ankle.
steps.find: Vibration is absent at both great toes, reduced at both medial malleoli and normal at the knees. Joint position sense is reduced at both great toes and normal at the ankles.

steps.do: Test the knee and ankle reflexes, with reinforcement if needed. Test the plantar responses.
steps.find: Ankle reflexes are absent on both sides, even with reinforcement. Knee reflexes are present and equal. Plantar responses are flexor on both sides.

steps.do: Test lower limb power at hip, knee, ankle and toes. Ask him to stand from a chair with his arms folded and to squat.
steps.find: Power 5/5 throughout. He stands from the chair with his arms folded and squats without difficulty, so there is no proximal myopathy.

bedside.find: 13.4 mmol/L, 2 hours after breakfast

bedside.test: Visual acuity (Snellen, each eye, with pinhole)
bedside.find: 6/9 in each eye, improving to 6/6 with pinhole. The retinal photograph is given in Part 2.
146/88 mmHg (first reading 148/90 mmHg), above the target of 130/80 mmHg or less

amsa-301.key: Jack has a symmetrical stocking-distribution sensory neuropathy: the monofilament is not felt, vibration is absent at the great toes and the ankle jerks are gone. That is loss of protective sensation, and the callus under the right first metatarsal head is high pressure on an insensate foot, a pre-ulcer sign. The left interdigital tinea breaks the skin barrier, so this is an at-risk foot. His pulses are palpable and the feet are warm, so there is no clinical evidence of peripheral arterial disease. The lipohypertrophy on his left thigh helps explain the erratic control and the hypos, and his BP is above the 130/80 target.

amsa-303.vitals: BP 112/70 mmHg, HR 88/min regular, RR 14/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C, weight 56 kg (about 59 kg a month ago), height 167 cm, BMI 20 kg/m2
amsa-303.general: Slim young woman who looks tired. She is comfortable at rest, alert and talks easily. No obvious jaundice and no distress.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for signs of anaemia, chronic liver disease and malabsorption, and look for a fine tremor with the arms outstretched (thyroid).
steps.find: No koilonychia, no clubbing, no palmar erythema and no tremor. Hands normal.

steps.do: Look for conjunctival pallor and scleral icterus. Inspect the corners of the mouth, the tongue and the oral mucosa for nutritional deficiency and ulcers.
steps.find: Mild conjunctival pallor. Angular cheilitis at both corners of the mouth. Tongue normal, no glossitis. No mouth ulcers. No jaundice.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the thyroid from behind, auscultate for a bruit, and check for lid lag and exophthalmos.
steps.find: Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules and no bruit. No lid lag and no exophthalmos.

steps.do: Palpate the cervical and supraclavicular nodes (including Virchow's node).
steps.find: No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart for a flow murmur from anaemia, and auscultate the chest.
steps.find: Heart sounds dual and normal, no murmurs. Chest clear, with equal air entry on both sides.

steps.do: Inspect, palpate lightly then deeply in all regions, check for masses and liver and spleen enlargement, and auscultate the bowel sounds.
steps.find: Mildly distended and soft. Mild periumbilical tenderness without guarding or rebound. No masses and no hepatosplenomegaly. Bowel sounds active. No scars.

steps.do: Offer a digital rectal examination with a chaperone, if indicated.
steps.find: Not needed today.

steps.do: With consent and a chaperone, examine both knees, then the elbows, buttocks and scalp (the extensor sites of dermatitis herpetiformis), the flexures (eczema), and look for bruising.
steps.find: Symmetrical clusters of small blisters with scratched, crusted bumps on a red background over the extensor surfaces of both knees. Elbows, buttocks and scalp clear. Elbow and knee creases clear, with no dry or thickened skin. No bruising.

bedside.find: 5.4 mmol/L, normal
Serum beta-hCG sent with the bloods; the result is given in Part 2

bedside.test: Weight and BMI compared with before
bedside.find: 56 kg, BMI 20 kg/m2, down 3 kg from about 59 kg over the past month

amsa-303.key: The important findings are the itchy, symmetrical blisters on the extensor knees with clear flexures, which point to dermatitis herpetiformis rather than eczema, plus mild pallor, angular cheilitis, abdominal distension, periumbilical tenderness and a 3 kg weight loss. Together these suggest malabsorption, most likely coeliac disease with iron deficiency. A normal thyroid examination, no lymph nodes, no masses or organ enlargement, normal glucose and normal observations make hyperthyroidism, diabetes, cancer and acute illness less likely.

amsa-307.vitals: Arrival (10:12): HR 98 regular, BP 150/88 mmHg (left arm), RR 20/min, SpO2 96% on room air, temperature 36.6 °C, BGL 7.2 mmol/L, pain 10/10. After the nurse's report (about 7 minutes in): HR 112 regular, BP 96/60 mmHg (left arm), RR 26/min.
amsa-307.general: Propped up on the trolley on a cardiac monitor, with an IV cannula in place. He is pale, sweaty, distressed and restless, can't get comfortable, keeps pressing on his chest and speaks in short sentences. He is alert. No Marfanoid features: he isn't tall or thin, arm span is normal, palate is not high-arched and fingers are not long. After the nurse's report he looks grey and clammy and says he feels faint again. Lying him flat makes him feel slightly less faint, but he stays pale and clammy.

steps.do: Feel both radial pulses at the same time for rate, rhythm and volume, then compare the femoral pulses
steps.find: The right radial pulse is weaker than the left. Rate 98 and regular (112 and regular after the nurse's report). Both femoral pulses are palpable and equal.

steps.do: Measure the BP in the left arm and in the right arm and compare the systolic readings
steps.find: Left arm 150/88, right arm 118/72: the right arm is 32 mmHg lower systolic. After the nurse's report: left arm 96/60, right arm 72/48.

steps.do: Feel the temperature of the hands and check capillary refill
steps.find: Hands are cool. CRT 3 seconds (4 seconds after the nurse's report).

steps.do: Look at the JVP with him propped up at 45 degrees and measure pulsus paradoxus
steps.find: JVP 3 cm above the sternal angle. After the nurse's report the JVP is 6 cm above the sternal angle and pulsus paradoxus is about 14 mmHg.

steps.do: Feel for the apex beat and listen in all areas, including the left and right sternal edges with him sitting forward in held expiration, and listen for a rub
steps.find: Apex beat is not displaced. Dual heart sounds. There is a soft, blowing early diastolic murmur at the right and left sternal edges, loudest at the right sternal edge with him sitting forward in held expiration. No pericardial rub. After the nurse's report the heart sounds are softer.

steps.do: Count the respiratory rate, check the trachea and chest expansion, percuss and listen to both lungs, and press on the chest wall
steps.find: RR 20 (26 after the nurse's report). Trachea central, expansion equal, chest resonant on both sides, vesicular breath sounds, no crackles or wheeze. Chest wall not tender. Normal.

steps.do: Check conscious state, pupils, face and speech, and test power and sensation in all four limbs
steps.find: GCS 15, pupils equal and reactive, no facial droop, speech normal, power and sensation normal in all four limbs. Normal.

steps.do: Palpate for tenderness and a pulsatile mass, and feel for a palpable bladder
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, no pulsatile mass, bladder not palpable. Normal.

steps.do: Feel the temperature of the legs and the femoral, popliteal and foot pulses, and check the calves
steps.find: Legs warm. Femoral, popliteal and foot pulses present and equal on both sides. Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling. Normal.

bedside.find: 7.2 mmol/L
Sinus rhythm, 98/min, regular. Sinus tachycardia 112/min after the nurse's report.
Recorded at 10:15. The examiner gives it in Part 2.
Sent from the cannula at 10:18. Results are given in Part 2.
Before the BP falls, the ED consultant has been asked to do one urgently. After the BP falls, the consultant is coming now to do it. The result is given in Part 2.
The ED consultant has requested an urgent study. The report is given in Part 2.

amsa-307.key: The key signs of aortic dissection are a weak right radial pulse, a right arm systolic BP 32 mmHg lower than the left, and a new early diastolic murmur of aortic regurgitation loudest at the right sternal edge. Together with sudden tearing pain through to the back, these point to a dissection of the ascending aorta that involves the brachiocephalic trunk. Use the left arm BP, because the right arm reads low. When the BP falls to 96/60 with HR 112, a rising JVP, pulsus paradoxus of about 14 mmHg and softer heart sounds, think haemopericardium with early tamponade. This needs senior help and the cardiothoracic surgeons now, with no BP-lowering drugs and no antithrombotics. The normal chest, neurological, abdominal and leg findings make pneumothorax unlikely and show no malperfusion of the brain, gut or limbs.

amsa-308.vitals: Repeat set at 10:20: BP 146/92 mmHg, HR 98/min regular, RR 18/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 36.8 °C (at 10:02), alert, CRT 2 seconds, pain 10/10 (he says 11/10)
amsa-308.general: He is overweight (BMI 30), pale and sweaty, and in obvious pain, pressing a fist into the middle of his chest. He is mildly short of breath but can speak in full sentences. He is alert and frightened. His right index and middle fingers are tar-stained. There is no xanthelasma, no cyanosis and no peripheral oedema on inspection.

steps.do: Inspect the hands, feel the peripheral temperature, check capillary refill, then feel both radial pulses together and the radial and femoral pulses together
steps.find: Tar staining of the right index and middle fingers. Peripheries warm, CRT 2 seconds. Pulse 98/min, regular, normal volume. Radial pulses equal, with no radio-radial or radio-femoral delay.

steps.do: Measure the BP in the right and left arms to screen for aortic dissection
steps.find: Right arm 146/92 mmHg, left arm 144/90 mmHg. Equal, with no significant difference between the arms.

steps.do: Inspect the eyes and face, then measure the JVP with him sitting at 45 degrees
steps.find: Pale and sweaty. No xanthelasma or corneal arcus, no central cyanosis. JVP not raised.

steps.do: Inspect the chest, palpate for the apex beat, heaves and thrills, then auscultate all areas, including with the bell and with him sitting forward
steps.find: No scars. Apex beat not displaced, no heaves or thrills. Dual heart sounds, no added sounds (no S3 or S4), no murmurs (no ejection systolic murmur of aortic stenosis) and no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Palpate over the sternum, costochondral junctions and the area of pain
steps.find: Not tender. Pressing does not reproduce the pain. No rash.

steps.do: Check the trachea, chest expansion and percussion, then auscultate both lung fields, including the bases
steps.find: Trachea central, expansion equal, resonant throughout, vesicular breath sounds, no crackles or wheeze. No signs of heart failure, pneumothorax or consolidation.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen, including the epigastrium, and feel for a pulsatile mass
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, no epigastric tenderness, no pulsatile mass.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the calves and ankles for DVT and oedema, and feel the peripheral pulses
steps.find: Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling, no pitting ankle oedema. Peripheral pulses present. Crepitus in the left knee (known osteoarthritis).

bedside.find: 9.4 mmol/L
Recorded by the nurse at 10:08 during the pain. The examiner gives it to the candidate in Part 2.
Sinus rhythm at about 95 to 98/min, with no arrhythmia seen
Cannula in, and bloods sent at 10:10, including a hs-troponin, FBC, electrolytes and renal function, coagulation, HbA1c and lipids. Results come in Part 2.
10/10 at 10:02 and 10:20 (he says 11/10). Persisting and not relieved by 3 doses of GTN at home.

amsa-308.key: Markus is haemodynamically stable and not hypoxic, with no signs of heart failure, shock or a murmur. However, he is pale and sweaty, his ischaemic-type pain is ongoing, and his heart rate and BP are rising, so he needs analgesia, nitrates and a repeat ECG now. His arm BPs and radial pulses are equal and his pain is not reproduced on palpation, which makes aortic dissection and chest wall pain less likely. A normal examination does not exclude an acute coronary syndrome.

amsa-310.vitals: HR 84 bpm regular, BP 118/74 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.9 °C, weight 78 kg, height 165 cm (BMI 28.7 kg/m^2), pain 7/10
amsa-310.general: Comfortable at rest, alert and speaking in full sentences, a bit anxious. Walks in with a slight limp to the left. Not breathless, pale or sweaty. Overweight. Mild acne on the face. No peripheral cyanosis.

steps.do: Exposes both legs from groin to toes and compares the two sides for swelling, colour, redness, skin breaks, bites, bruising and collateral superficial veins.
steps.find: Left calf visibly swollen compared with the right. No redness, streaking, skin breaks, insect bites or bruising. No visible collateral (non-varicose) superficial veins. Both feet pink.

steps.do: Uses the back of the hand to compare temperature on both legs, then palpates gently along the deep veins of the calf, popliteal fossa and thigh on each side.
steps.find: Left calf slightly warmer than the right. Tender along the deep veins of the left calf and in the left popliteal fossa. No tenderness along the femoral vein in the thigh. Right leg not tender.

steps.do: Presses firmly for a few seconds over the ankles and lower shins on both sides, looking for pitting.
steps.find: Pitting oedema of the left ankle and lower shin. No oedema on the right.

steps.do: Measures calf circumference on both sides 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity, and compares thigh circumference.
steps.find: Calf circumference left 39.5 cm, right 36.0 cm (3.5 cm larger on the left). Thigh circumference the same on both sides, so the whole leg is not swollen.

steps.do: Palpates the left popliteal fossa for a mass or cyst and examines the knee for effusion and range of movement.
steps.find: No mass or cyst felt in the popliteal fossa. Knee has full range of movement, with no effusion.

steps.do: Palpates the gastrocnemius and soleus for a defect, tests resisted plantarflexion, does the Simmonds-Thompson test and watches her bear weight and walk.
steps.find: No palpable defect in the calf muscles. Mild pain on resisted plantarflexion. Simmonds-Thompson test normal (Achilles intact). Bears weight with a slight antalgic limp.

steps.do: Palpates the femoral, popliteal, dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on both sides, checks capillary refill, and tests sensation and power in both feet.
steps.find: All pulses present and equal on both sides. Capillary refill under 2 seconds on both sides. Sensation and power normal in both legs.

steps.do: Palpates the inguinal lymph nodes on both sides.
steps.find: No inguinal lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Checks the JVP, auscultates the heart and both lung fields, and looks for a pleural rub.
steps.find: JVP not raised. Heart sounds dual with no added sounds and no loud P2. Chest clear with normal breath sounds throughout and no pleural rub.

bedside.find: Negative.
Normal: no blood, protein, leucocytes or nitrites.
5.4 mmol/L.
Sinus rhythm at 84 bpm, normal axis, normal intervals. No right heart strain pattern (no S1Q3T3, no right bundle branch block, no T-wave inversion in V1 to V4).

amsa-310.key: Mary has a swollen, warm left calf that is 3.5 cm bigger than the right, with pitting oedema and tenderness along the deep veins. That gives a Wells score of 3 (DVT likely), so she goes straight to compression ultrasound rather than a D-dimer. Her pulses are normal, there is no defect in the calf muscle, no cyst behind the knee and no redness or skin break, which makes arterial disease, a muscle tear, a Baker's cyst and cellulitis less likely. Her observations, chest examination and ECG are normal, so there are no clinical signs of PE, and with a negative pregnancy test she is stable for outpatient workup.

amsa-323.vitals: 14:00: Temp 37.5 °C, HR 92 bpm regular, BP 126/78 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air, capillary BGL 5.4 mmol/L, pain 3/10. Weight 82 kg, height 180 cm (BMI 25.3 kg/m²).
amsa-323.general: Comfortable lying still in bed. Alert, fully oriented and talking in full sentences, not drowsy. Not pale, jaundiced or flushed. Peripheral cannula in the left forearm with a clean site and nothing running.
