steps.find: Bruising and an abrasion over the left lateral chest. Tender over the left lateral ribs. No crepitus, no surgical emphysema, no flail segment and no open or sucking wound.

steps.do: Assess chest expansion on both sides and percuss both hemithoraces from front to back
steps.find: Reduced expansion on the left. Hyper-resonant to percussion over the whole left chest. Normal expansion on the right, which is resonant.

steps.do: Auscultate both lungs, front and back
steps.find: Breath sounds reduced over the whole left lung. Right lung: vesicular breath sounds with no added sounds. No wheeze on either side.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart sounds
steps.find: Heart sounds present and not muffled. Tachycardic with no murmur and no pericardial rub.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the abdomen, including the left upper quadrant for splenic injury
steps.find: Soft and non-tender, including the left upper quadrant. No guarding and no bruising. Well-healed appendicectomy scar.

steps.do: Assess conscious level and palpate the cervical spine
steps.find: Alert, GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6). No cervical spine tenderness. Moving all four limbs normally.

steps.do: Inspect the legs for injury and examine the calves for DVT
steps.find: Grazes on the left thigh. Calves soft and non-tender, with no swelling.

bedside.find: Sinus tachycardia at 134 bpm. Normal axis, no ST or T wave changes, no low voltage and no electrical alternans.
7.1 mmol/L
7/10, left lateral chest, worse on breathing in

amsa-630.key: This is a left tension pneumothorax causing obstructive shock. He has distended neck veins and a trachea pushed to the right. His left chest moves less, is hyper-resonant and has reduced breath sounds, and he is hypotensive, tachycardic and hypoxic. The heart sounds are clear, which points away from tamponade. The left chest is hyper-resonant rather than dull, and the neck veins are full rather than flat, which points away from haemothorax. Rib tenderness alone cannot explain the shift or the shock. This is a clinical diagnosis, so it needs high-flow oxygen, a senior doctor and immediate left-sided decompression now, without waiting for the chest X-ray.

amsa-631.vitals: RR 46/min, SpO2 93% on room air, HR 158/min regular, BP 96/60 mmHg, temperature 37.8 °C, central CRT 2 seconds, alert (AVPU A), weight 15 kg (triage at 06:40: RR 44, SpO2 94%, HR 155, BP 98/62)
amsa-631.general: Alert 3-year-old boy, a bit grizzly but settles on his mother's lap. Sitting upright and breathing fast. Talking in short sentences, a little less than usual for him. Pink, not cyanosed. Clear nasal discharge. No drooling, no stridor, normal voice. Not tripoding. Well grown (15 kg, about the 65th centile).

steps.do: Counts the respiratory rate and looks for tracheal tug, subcostal and intercostal recession, nasal flaring, accessory muscle use, head bobbing and grunting
steps.find: RR 46/min. Moderate subcostal and intercostal recession with some abdominal breathing. No tracheal tug, no nasal flaring, no head bobbing, no grunting.

steps.do: Inspects chest shape and symmetry, checks tracheal position and chest expansion
steps.find: Chest looks slightly hyperexpanded. Trachea central. Expansion equal on both sides.

steps.do: Percusses both sides of the chest, front and back
steps.find: Resonant throughout on both sides. No dullness.

steps.do: Listens to both lungs, front and back, comparing sides for air entry and added sounds
steps.find: Widespread high-pitched expiratory wheeze on both sides with a prolonged expiratory phase. Good, equal air entry on both sides; not a silent chest. No focal crackles, no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Checks heart rate and rhythm, peripheral temperature and central capillary refill, and listens to the heart
steps.find: HR 158/min, regular. Warm peripheries, central CRT 2 seconds. Heart sounds normal, no murmur.

steps.do: Checks mucous membranes, eyes and skin turgor
steps.find: Lips slightly dry, tongue moist, eyes not sunken, normal skin turgor. Not clinically dehydrated.

steps.do: Inspects the skin for urticaria, angioedema, petechiae and eczema
steps.find: Dry, slightly rough eczema patches in both elbow and knee creases. No urticaria, no lip, face or tongue swelling, no petechiae or purpura.

steps.area: Ears, nose and throat, and neck
steps.do: Examines the throat and ear drums and feels the cervical lymph nodes
steps.find: Clear nasal discharge. Mildly red throat, tonsils not enlarged, no exudate. Ear drums normal on both sides. A few small, soft, non-tender cervical lymph nodes.

steps.do: Palpates the abdomen
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No masses, no organomegaly.

bedside.find: SpO2 93% on room air at 06:55 (94% at triage). Above 92%, so no oxygen is needed yet. Trend is slightly worse.

bedside.test: Reassessment 20 minutes after salbutamol 6 puffs (100 microgram/puff) by spacer and mask, if given
bedside.find: RR 40/min, SpO2 95% on room air, HR 156/min. Less recession, but mild subcostal recession and wheeze remain. A little more settled. Heart rate still fast because of the salbutamol; otherwise improving.

bedside.test: Nasopharyngeal swab for respiratory viral PCR
bedside.find: Taken at triage and sent to the lab. The result will be given in Part 2.

bedside.test: Chest X-ray or bloods, if asked for
bedside.find: Results will be given in Part 2 (not routinely indicated).

amsa-631.key: Wesley has a moderate episode: he is alert, has moderate subcostal and intercostal recession, talks in short sentences and has SpO2 93–94% in air, with widespread bilateral expiratory wheeze and good, equal air entry. This fits viral-induced wheeze and needs salbutamol by spacer now, with senior review because his observations are in the yellow zone and getting slightly worse. Several findings argue against the dangerous differentials: no urticaria or angioedema (against anaphylaxis), symmetrical signs with no focal crackles or bronchial breathing (against an inhaled foreign body or pneumonia), and no stridor or drooling (against croup or epiglottitis). He is well perfused and not clinically dehydrated.

amsa-632.vitals: Repeat set at 10:50 on room air: RR 34/min, SpO2 86% on room air, HR 114/min regular, BP 212/112 mmHg, Temp 36.8 °C, capillary refill 3 s, alert (A on AVPU), BGL 7.2 mmol/L (triage 10:42: RR 32, SpO2 87%, HR 108, BP 206/108). Weight 88 kg. With oxygen, SpO2 rises to about 92%. After GTN, BP falls to about 160/90 mmHg and HR to about 104/min.
amsa-632.general: 73-year-old man sitting bolt upright on the trolley, in severe respiratory distress. He is using his neck and shoulder muscles to breathe and can only say 3 or 4 words at a time. He is sweaty and frightened, with dusky lips. A tissue in his hand holds pink frothy sputum. He is on a cardiac monitor with an IV cannula in place. He will not lie flat: "Don't lie me down, I can't breathe flat."

steps.do: Inspect and feel the hands, check capillary refill, look for clubbing and peripheral stigmata
steps.find: Cool and clammy hands, capillary refill 3 seconds. No clubbing. Nicotine staining of the right fingers. Small healed puncture mark at the right wrist (radial angiogram access).

steps.do: Palpate the radial pulse for rate, rhythm and volume, and compare both sides
steps.find: 114/min (about 104/min after GTN), regular, normal volume. No radio-radial delay.

steps.do: Check the blood pressure (manual or from the monitor)
steps.find: 212/112 mmHg before treatment (about 160/90 mmHg after GTN). Severely hypertensive.

steps.do: Inspect the lips and tongue for cyanosis, then assess the JVP with him sitting upright
steps.find: Dusky lips. JVP raised, 5 cm above the sternal angle with him sitting upright.

steps.do: Inspect, then palpate for the apex beat, heaves and thrills
steps.find: Apex beat displaced to the 6th intercostal space, anterior axillary line. No parasternal heave, no thrills. No chest wall trauma.

steps.do: Auscultate all four valve areas, listening for added sounds, murmurs and a rub
steps.find: S1 and S2 with an added third heart sound (gallop rhythm). No murmurs. No pericardial rub.

steps.do: Check tracheal position, chest expansion, percussion and auscultation front and back (sitting forward with support, keeping him upright)
steps.find: Trachea central. Expansion reduced at both bases. Dull to percussion at both bases, resonant above. Breath sounds reduced at both bases. Fine inspiratory crackles over both lungs from the bases up to the mid zones. No wheeze, no bronchial breathing.

steps.do: Palpate for tenderness, the liver and an aortic mass
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. Liver not palpable. No pulsatile mass.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the lumbar spine and paraspinal muscles, and check for sacral oedema
steps.find: Tender lumbar paraspinal muscles. No midline bony tenderness. No sacral oedema.

steps.do: Check both ankles for pitting oedema, the calves for DVT and the foot pulses
steps.find: Trace pitting oedema at both ankles. Calves soft and non-tender, no swelling. Foot pulses present on both sides.

bedside.find: 7.2 mmol/L
Regular narrow complex tachycardia at about 110 to 114/min, no ectopics seen
Room air SpO2 86%, rising to about 92% on titrated oxygen, but he is still very breathless
Pink, frothy, watery sputum in the tissue. Not purulent, no frank blood.

bedside.test: 12-lead ECG, venous blood gas and bloods
bedside.find: ECG recorded and bloods with a venous gas sent. The examiner will give the results in Part 2.
Requested. The examiner will give the report in Part 2.

amsa-632.key: He has severe, worsening hypoxaemic respiratory distress (RR 34 and SpO2 86% on room air) with marked hypertension. He needs sitting upright, oxygen to a target of 92 to 96%, nitrates and senior help straight away. The raised JVP, S3, displaced apex, bilateral crackles to the mid zones and bibasal dullness (effusions) point to acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema from left ventricular failure after his recent MI. The afebrile, regular rhythm, clear sputum and soft calves argue against pneumonia, AF and PE.

amsa-633.vitals: RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air, BP 128/78 mmHg, HR 104 bpm regular, temperature 38.6 °C, alert, pain 8/10, BGL 6.1 mmol/L. Weight 88 kg, height 165 cm (BMI about 32).
amsa-633.general: Uncomfortable, lying still on the trolley and avoiding movement. Flushed and sweaty. Alert and oriented. Obese body habitus. IV cannula in place.

steps.do: Inspect the hands, feel the temperature of the peripheries and check capillary refill
steps.find: Warm peripheries, CRT 2 seconds. No stigmata of chronic liver disease (no palmar erythema, leuconychia, clubbing or asterixis).

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae and skin for jaundice and the mucous membranes for hydration
steps.find: Sclerae not yellow, no jaundice. Mucous membranes slightly dry. No spider naevi or scratch marks.

steps.do: Inspect the exposed abdomen with the patient lying flat
steps.find: Not distended, moves normally with breathing. Healed appendicectomy scar in the right iliac fossa. No visible masses.

steps.do: Palpate all nine regions, starting away from the pain and watching her face
steps.find: Marked tenderness in the right upper quadrant with voluntary guarding. Mild epigastric discomfort. No tenderness elsewhere. No rebound tenderness, no rigidity. No masses.

steps.do: Press below the right costal margin in the mid-clavicular line while she breathes in, then compare the left side
steps.find: Murphy's sign positive: she stops breathing in when the gallbladder area is pressed. No catch on the left.

steps.do: Palpate for the liver, gallbladder, spleen and kidneys
steps.find: Liver not enlarged. Gallbladder not palpable. Spleen and kidneys not palpable.

steps.area: Percussion and auscultation of the abdomen
steps.do: Percuss for tenderness and shifting dullness, then listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: No percussion tenderness away from the right upper quadrant. No shifting dullness. Bowel sounds present and normal.

steps.do: Press over the renal angles and check the inguinal and femoral hernial orifices
steps.find: Renal angles not tender. Hernial orifices normal.

steps.do: Check chest expansion, percuss and auscultate the lungs including the right base, then auscultate the heart
steps.find: Equal expansion, resonant, clear breath sounds including the right base. Dual heart sounds, no murmurs.

steps.do: Offer a rectal or pelvic examination
steps.find: The examiner says it is not needed.

bedside.find: 6.1 mmol/L
Sinus tachycardia 104/min, no ST or T wave changes.
Negative for blood, leucocytes, nitrites and bilirubin.
Bloods have been sent; results and the ultrasound are given in Part 2.

amsa-633.key: Fever of 38.6 °C, tachycardia, and right upper quadrant tenderness with guarding and a positive Murphy's sign point to acute cholecystitis rather than biliary colic. She has no jaundice and no signs of generalised peritonitis, and her BP and perfusion are normal, so she is septic-looking but not shocked. A clear right lung base, a normal ECG, a negative urine dipstick and non-tender renal angles make pneumonia, ACS and a renal cause less likely.

amsa-634.vitals: HR 108 bpm regular, BP 118/76 mmHg, RR 18 breaths/min, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 37.4 °C, BGL 5.8 mmol/L
amsa-634.general: Uncomfortable woman lying on the trolley. With each wave of cramping pain she curls up and stops talking, then settles between waves. Bilious green-yellow vomit in the bowl beside her. Alert and talking in full sentences.

steps.do: Inspect the mucous membranes, check capillary refill centrally and peripherally, and feel the temperature of the peripheries
steps.find: Dry mucous membranes. CRT 2 seconds. Warm peripheries.

steps.do: Look for pallor, jaundice and stigmata of chronic disease, and palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes, including Virchow's node
steps.find: No pallor, no jaundice. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Expose the abdomen from nipples to knees with the patient lying flat. Look for distension, scars and visible peristalsis
steps.find: Mildly distended. Well-healed Pfannenstiel scar and a right iliac fossa (gridiron) scar. No visible peristalsis.

steps.do: Examine the inguinal, femoral and umbilical regions and both scars for incisional hernia, with a cough impulse
steps.find: No inguinal, femoral, umbilical or incisional hernia. Cough impulse negative.

steps.do: Palpate gently, watching her face, then deeply across all regions for tenderness, guarding, rigidity, rebound, masses and organomegaly
steps.find: Mild diffuse tenderness, worst around the umbilicus. No guarding, rigidity or rebound tenderness. No masses. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly.

steps.do: Percuss across the abdomen and test for shifting dullness
steps.find: Tympanic centrally. No shifting dullness.

steps.do: Auscultate for bowel sounds for at least 30 seconds
steps.find: High-pitched, tinkling bowel sounds.

steps.do: Request a PR examination with consent and a chaperone
steps.find: Empty rectum. No blood on the glove. No mass felt.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and lungs
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, tachycardic. Chest clear with good air entry on both sides.

bedside.find: 5.8 mmol/L
She has not passed urine since she arrived, so no sample is available yet. Serum beta-hCG has been sent with the bloods (result in Part 2).
Small residual volume, about 80 mL, consistent with low urine output rather than retention.
Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm. Normal axis and intervals, QTc normal. No ischaemic changes.

amsa-634.key: The findings that matter are tinkling bowel sounds, a mildly distended tympanic abdomen and bilious vomiting in a woman with Pfannenstiel and gridiron scars. Together these point to small bowel obstruction, most likely from adhesions. Her tachycardia and dry mucous membranes show significant fluid loss. The normal hernial orifices and the absence of guarding, rigidity or rebound make an incarcerated hernia or established strangulation less likely. They do not rule out ischaemia, so she needs close re-examination.

amsa-635.vitals: HR 96 regular, BP 132/80 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 37.8 °C, BGL 5.6 mmol/L (triage set at 10:40)
amsa-635.general: Tired, irritable 40-year-old man who keeps scratching his arms and chest. Visibly jaundiced. Alert and fully oriented to time, place and person. Speaking in full sentences, not distressed at rest, well perfused.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms, then test for asterixis with the arms outstretched and wrists dorsiflexed
steps.find: No clubbing, leuconychia, palmar erythema or Dupuytren's contracture. No asterixis.

steps.do: Inspect the skin of the trunk and limbs and both antecubital fossae for injection sites
steps.find: Raised, red, blanching wheals (urticaria) over the trunk and limbs, with scratch marks. A few healing puncture marks in the left antecubital fossa, with no abscess, cellulitis or thrombophlebitis. No spider naevi, bruising or petechiae.

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae in good light and check conscious state and orientation
steps.find: Yellow sclerae (scleral icterus). Alert and fully oriented, with no confusion or drowsiness.

steps.do: Inspect for gynaecomastia and loss of body hair, and palpate the cervical, supraclavicular and axillary nodes
steps.find: No gynaecomastia and normal body hair. No lymphadenopathy.

steps.do: Inspect and move the large and small joints, including the knees and wrists
steps.find: Knees and wrists ache on movement. No swelling, warmth or effusion.

steps.do: Inspect the abdomen with the patient lying flat
steps.find: Not distended. No caput medusae, scars or visible veins.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply, palpate the liver and spleen, test Murphy's sign, ballot the kidneys and check for guarding and rebound
steps.find: Tender in the right upper quadrant. The liver edge is smooth, soft and tender, 3 cm below the right costal margin. Murphy's sign negative. No guarding or rebound. Spleen not palpable and kidneys not ballotable.

steps.do: Percuss the liver span, test for shifting dullness and listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: Liver span 15 cm. No shifting dullness. Normal bowel sounds.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and the lung fields, including both bases
steps.find: Normal heart sounds with no murmurs. Chest clear at both bases.

steps.do: Perform a digital rectal examination and inspect the glove
steps.find: Pale, clay-coloured stool on the glove. No blood or melaena.

bedside.find: Dark, tea-coloured urine. Bilirubin 2+. No blood, leucocytes or nitrites.
5.6 mmol/L
Sinus rhythm at 96/min, normal axis and intervals, no ST or T wave changes.
Results will be given in Part 2.

amsa-635.key: Andrew is jaundiced with a low-grade fever, urticaria, and a smooth, tender liver 3 cm below the costal margin. Murphy's sign is negative, the urine contains bilirubin and the stool is pale, which together point to acute hepatitis rather than gallbladder disease. Fever, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice make up Charcot's triad, so cholangitis still has to be ruled out in Part 2. He is alert with no asterixis, a normal BGL and no stigmata of chronic liver disease, so there is no sign of acute liver failure or chronic liver disease. The healing puncture marks in his left antecubital fossa back up the needle-sharing history as the likely route of infection.

amsa-636.vitals: HR 112 bpm regular, BP 110/80 mmHg (usual about 150/90), RR 18 /min, SpO2 96% on room air, temperature 36.9 °C, CRT 3 seconds, BGL 6.8 mmol/L. Weight about 82 kg.
amsa-636.general: Older man lying on the trolley with a vomit bowl beside him. Conscious, alert and oriented. Pale, frightened and distressed about the bleeding. He speaks in full sentences and is not short of breath at rest. No fresh blood in the vomit bowl at the moment. No jaundice.

steps.do: Feel the temperature of the hands, measure capillary refill, and look at the nails and palms for stigmata of chronic liver disease. Check for asterixis.
steps.find: Cool hands. CRT 3 seconds. No clubbing, leuconychia, palmar erythema or Dupuytren's contracture. No asterixis. Radial pulse 112, regular, low volume.

steps.do: Look at the conjunctivae and sclerae and inspect the mucous membranes.
steps.find: Conjunctival pallor. Sclerae not yellow. Mucous membranes dry. No parotid enlargement.

steps.do: Look for the JVP and palpate the carotid pulses.
steps.find: JVP not seen with the patient lying at 45 degrees. Carotid pulses normal and equal.

steps.do: Inspect the chest for spider naevi, gynaecomastia and loss of body hair.
steps.find: A single spider naevus on the left upper chest. No gynaecomastia. No other stigmata of chronic liver disease.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart, then the lungs including the bases.
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, tachycardic, no murmur. Good air entry throughout, no basal crackles or wheeze.

steps.do: Inspect for distension, scars and caput medusae. Palpate gently, starting away from the pain, and look for peritonism. Feel for the liver, spleen and any masses.
steps.find: Not distended. No caput medusae and no scars. Soft. Tender in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant, with voluntary guarding there. No rigidity. Liver and spleen not palpable. No masses.

steps.do: Percuss for tenderness and shifting dullness, and auscultate for bowel sounds.
steps.find: Percussion tenderness in the epigastrium. No shifting dullness. Normal bowel sounds.

steps.do: Palpate deeply above the umbilicus for an expansile mass.
steps.find: Aorta normal and not expansile.

steps.do: Digital rectal examination with consent and a chaperone, or document it later if the melaena stool on the bedpan has already confirmed it.
steps.find: Black, tarry stool staining around the anus. No haemorrhoids or fissures. Normal anal tone. No masses. Black, tarry, foul-smelling melaena on the glove with no fresh red blood. (The nurse also reports a large, loose, black, tarry stool on the bedpan.)

steps.do: Ask for lying and standing blood pressure.
steps.find: Not done. The nurse says he is on bed rest. They are not needed: the resting tachycardia already shows significant volume loss, and standing him risks a faint.

bedside.find: 6.8 mmol/L
Large, loose, black, tarry, foul-smelling stool, which is melaena. No fresh red blood.
Not available. He has passed no urine since arriving about 20 minutes ago and has no IDC. An IDC is needed to measure output.
Sinus tachycardia at about 112 bpm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST or T wave changes.

amsa-636.key: At rest he has a tachycardia of 112 and a BP of 110/80 (usual about 150/90), with a narrow pulse pressure, cool peripheries, a CRT of 3 seconds, pallor and ongoing melaena. This is compensated hypovolaemic shock from an active upper GI bleed, even though his chart is in the white zone. Apart from one spider naevus there are no stigmata of chronic liver disease, which argues against varices. The epigastric and right upper quadrant guarding with percussion tenderness raises the possibility of a perforation, so he needs an erect chest X-ray, a surgical review and a low threshold for CT before gastroscopy.

amsa-637.vitals: Temperature 37.8 °C, HR 92 bpm regular, BP 116/72 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, capillary BGL 5.2 mmol/L, weight 62 kg
amsa-637.general: Alert and fully oriented young woman. She looks tired but is not distressed. She has obvious scleral icterus and a faint yellow tinge to her skin in natural light. There are scratch marks on both forearms. No bruising or petechiae.

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae in natural light, then the skin, looking for jaundice, excoriations, bruising, petechiae and rash
steps.find: Obvious scleral icterus and a faint yellow tinge to the skin. Scratch marks on both forearms, in keeping with pruritus. No bruising, petechiae or rash.

steps.do: Check the mucous membranes and capillary refill time
steps.find: Mucous membranes moist, CRT under 2 seconds. Clinically well hydrated.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for signs of chronic liver disease, then test for asterixis with the arms out and wrists extended
steps.find: No clubbing, leuconychia, palmar erythema or Dupuytren's contracture. No asterixis.

steps.do: Assess conscious state, orientation and attention for hepatic encephalopathy
steps.find: Alert and oriented to time, place and person. No confusion or drowsiness.

steps.do: Look for spider naevi and palpate the cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes
steps.find: No spider naevi. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. No rash.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and the lung fields
steps.find: Heart sounds dual, no murmurs. Chest clear on both sides.

steps.do: Inspect, then palpate lightly and deeply in all quadrants, noting tenderness, guarding and masses
steps.find: Not distended, no scars or distended veins. Tender in the right upper quadrant with no guarding. No masses.

steps.do: Palpate and percuss the liver edge from the right iliac fossa, test Murphy's sign, and palpate for the spleen
steps.find: Smooth, soft, tender liver edge palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin. Murphy's sign negative. Spleen not palpable.

steps.do: Percuss for shifting dullness and auscultate for bowel sounds
steps.find: No shifting dullness. Bowel sounds normal.

bedside.find: Bilirubin 2+, urobilinogen not increased. Blood, leucocytes, nitrites and protein negative.
Negative
5.2 mmol/L

amsa-637.key: She is jaundiced with a low-grade fever, scratch marks from itch, a smooth tender liver 2 cm below the costal margin and bilirubin in her urine. This fits conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia from an acute hepatitis. Murphy's sign is negative, and there is no guarding or splenomegaly, which makes cholecystitis or cholangitis less likely. She has no asterixis or confusion, no bruising, no ascites and no signs of chronic liver disease, so there is no sign of acute liver failure and she can be managed at home while results are pending. Her pregnancy test is negative.

amsa-638.vitals: RR 18/min, SpO2 98% on room air, BP 112/70 mmHg, HR 112 bpm regular, Temp 38.7 °C, alert (AVPU A), pain 8/10, BGL 5.8 mmol/L, height 165 cm, weight 62 kg
amsa-638.general: Unwell young woman lying on the trolley holding her right upper quadrant. She is flushed and sweaty, and in obvious pain with each wave. Her skin is obviously jaundiced, with a few faint scratch marks on both forearms. She is alert and oriented to time, place and person, not confused, and chatty between waves of pain. Partway through, the nurse reports that she has started shaking uncontrollably (rigors) and feels very hot.

steps.do: Check orientation to time, place and person and look for drowsiness or confusion
steps.find: Alert and fully oriented to time, place and person. Not confused or drowsy.

steps.do: Inspect the mucous membranes, measure capillary refill and feel the peripheries
steps.find: Mucous membranes slightly dry. CRT 2 seconds. Warm peripheries.

steps.do: Inspect the sclerae for jaundice and the conjunctivae for pallor
steps.find: Yellow sclerae. No conjunctival pallor.

steps.do: Look for stigmata of chronic liver disease and test for asterixis
steps.find: No clubbing, leuconychia or palmar erythema. No spider naevi. No asterixis. Faint scratch marks on the forearms.

steps.do: Inspect the exposed abdomen for distension, scars and visible masses
steps.find: Not distended. Healed right iliac fossa appendicectomy scar. No other scars and no visible mass.

steps.do: Palpate gently, starting away from the pain, then palpate deeply. Check for rebound and rigidity and test Murphy's sign
steps.find: Tender in the right upper quadrant with mild voluntary guarding. No rebound tenderness and no rigidity. Murphy's sign negative. Rest of the abdomen soft and non-tender. No masses.

steps.do: Palpate and percuss for the liver, gallbladder and spleen
steps.find: Liver edge just palpable at the costal margin, smooth and tender, not enlarged. Gallbladder not palpable. Spleen not palpable.

steps.do: Percuss for shifting dullness and listen for bowel sounds
steps.find: No shifting dullness. Bowel sounds present and normal.

steps.do: Palpate the renal angles and check the hernial orifices
steps.find: Renal angles not tender. Hernial orifices normal. Rectal and pelvic examination not needed (examiner).

steps.do: Examine chest expansion, percuss and auscultate the lungs, including the right base, and auscultate the heart
steps.find: Equal expansion, resonant to percussion and clear breath sounds throughout, including the right base. Dual heart sounds, no murmurs. Tachycardic and regular.

bedside.find: Bilirubin 3+, urobilinogen negative. No blood, leucocytes or nitrites.
5.8 mmol/L
Serum beta-hCG sent with the triage bloods; the result comes with the other bloods in Part 2.
Results will be given in Part 2.

amsa-638.key: She has Charcot's triad: right upper quadrant pain, fever (38.7 °C) with rigors, and jaundice with yellow sclerae. Together with tachycardia, this means suspected sepsis from acute cholangitis, so she needs cultures, antibiotics and fluids without delay. Urine with bilirubin 3+ and no urobilinogen, with pale stools and itch, points to obstructive (post-hepatic) jaundice. Murphy's sign is negative and there are no stigmata of chronic liver disease, which make cholecystitis and chronic liver disease less likely. She is alert and not confused, so there is no sign of Reynolds' pentad yet.

amsa-644.vitals: In cardiac arrest: no carotid pulse, not breathing normally (one slow agonal gasp in 10 seconds), BP and SpO2 not recordable (no monitoring attached), GCS 3. Last ward observations at 09:30 were RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air, BP 132/80, HR 78 regular, temperature 36.7 °C, alert, pain 0/10.
amsa-644.general: Collin is a 64-year-old man, half sitting up in bed and slumped to the left. He is grey with his eyes half open and makes no spontaneous movement. A 20 G IV cannula is in his left forearm. No cardiac monitor, oxygen or other equipment is attached. Sam, the third-year student, is at the bedside and is distressed. The Code Blue was called at 10:42 and the team is on its way.

steps.do: Check the bed space for electrical, fluid, sharps and oxygen hazards. Lay the electric bed flat with the backrest down and place a CPR board under him.
steps.find: No hazards. The floor is dry, the electric bed works normally, no oxygen is running and there are no sharps. The bed lays flat and a CPR board is on the resuscitation trolley.

steps.do: Talk and touch: "Collin, can you hear me? Open your eyes. Squeeze my hand," with a firm shoulder squeeze, then trapezius or sternal pressure.
steps.find: No response to voice, shoulder squeeze, or trapezius or sternal pressure. He is unresponsive.

steps.do: Confirm the Code Blue has been called and ask for the defibrillator and resuscitation trolley (for example, send Sam or RN Kate Nguyen to get them).
steps.find: The Code Blue was called at 10:42 and the team is coming. The defibrillator and trolley arrive about a minute after they are asked for.

steps.do: Head tilt and chin lift (or jaw thrust), look in the mouth for foreign material, listen, suction with a Yankauer, then insert an oropharyngeal (Guedel) airway sized from the angle of the mandible to the centre of the incisors.
steps.find: No visible foreign body. Gurgling with secretions at the back of the mouth, so the airway is not patent. Yankauer suction clears the secretions. Once the Guedel is in place, the airway is patent.

steps.do: Look, listen and feel for no more than 10 seconds, with a carotid pulse check at the same time if wanted.
steps.find: Not breathing normally: one slow, noisy agonal gasp only. No carotid pulse. This is cardiac arrest.

steps.do: Start compressions straight away on the lower half of the sternum at 100 to 120 a minute, to one third of the chest depth, with full recoil. Give 30:2 with a bag-valve-mask on oxygen at 15 L/min. Rotate the person doing compressions every 2 minutes.
steps.find: Compressions are effective on the CPR board. The chest rises with each bag-valve-mask breath. There is no spontaneous movement or breathing.

steps.do: Apply the pads in the anterolateral position (below the right clavicle, and the left mid-axillary line at V6) while compressions continue. Pause only for the AED analysis, make sure everyone is clear and the oxygen is moved away, shock, then restart CPR straight away.
steps.find: AED analysis at 10:44: "Shock advised. Stand clear." Once everyone is clear, a 200 J biphasic shock is delivered and the AED says "Shock delivered. Start CPR."

steps.do: Restart compressions straight away for 2 minutes, with no pulse or rhythm check until the next analysis.
steps.find: No change. Collin remains unresponsive, without normal breathing, and CPR continues.

steps.do: Check and flush the existing cannula, or ask for intraosseous access if it fails.
steps.find: The 20 G cannula in the left forearm flushes easily and can be used for drugs.

bedside.find: Shock advised. One 200 J biphasic shock was delivered at 10:44, followed by "Start CPR". The formal rhythm strip is given in Part 2.
The chest rises with each breath once the Guedel is in place and the secretions are suctioned.
The 20 G left forearm cannula is patent and flushes easily.
Sinus rhythm at 80 to 84/min with 1 to 2 mm ST depression in V4 to V6, I and aVL and no ST elevation. The 06:00 ECG is unchanged from admission.

bedside.test: 12-lead ECG, capillary glucose and blood gas now
bedside.find: Not done during BLS, as they must not interrupt CPR. A venous gas taken during CPR and the morning bloods are given in Part 2.

amsa-644.key: Collin is unresponsive and pulseless with only agonal gasps, which is a witnessed cardiac arrest. Compressions should start at once, and the gasps and brief jerks must not be mistaken for breathing or a seizure. The AED advises a shock, which fits a shockable rhythm (VF) from acute ischaemia in a man with an evolving NSTEMI whose chest pain came back just before he collapsed. Early defibrillation with minimal pauses in compressions is the intervention most likely to help him.

amsa-645.vitals: RR 18/min, SpO2 97% on room air, BP 118/72 mmHg, HR 112 bpm regular, temperature 38.9 °C, CRT 2 seconds, pain 7/10, weight 78 kg
amsa-645.general: Flushed, sweaty and unwell. He lies still on the trolley with his eyes half closed and moves his head as little as possible. Photophobic: he winces at bright light and loud noise. Alert and answering clearly, though slowly and with effort. Dry mucous membranes.

steps.do: Assess the GCS by components, orientation to time, place and person, and attention (months of the year backwards)
steps.find: GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6). Oriented to time, place and person. Attention intact: says the months backwards correctly. Not drowsy or confused.

steps.do: Inspect the whole skin for a petechial or purpuric non-blanching rash, including the trunk, limbs, palms, soles and conjunctivae
steps.find: No rash, petechiae or purpura anywhere, including the trunk, legs, palms, soles and conjunctivae.

steps.do: Test passive neck flexion, Kernig's sign and Brudzinski's sign, and look for photophobia
steps.find: Marked neck stiffness: resists passive neck flexion. Kernig's sign positive. Brudzinski's sign positive. Photophobic.

steps.do: Check pupil size, symmetry and light reflexes, then do fundoscopy with the lights dimmed
steps.find: Pupils 4 mm, equal and reactive to light. Optic discs sharp, no papilloedema.

steps.do: Screen visual fields, eye movements, facial symmetry, hearing to whisper, palate and tongue
steps.find: Visual fields full. Eye movements full with no diplopia or nystagmus. Face symmetrical. Hearing normal to whisper. Palate and tongue normal.

steps.do: Assess tone, power, reflexes, sensation, pronator drift, coordination and plantar responses in all four limbs
steps.find: Tone, power (5/5), reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical. No pronator drift. Coordination normal. Plantars flexor. Gait not tested because he is too unwell to stand.

steps.area: Head, ears, nose and throat and hydration
steps.do: Look for head injury, examine the tympanic membranes and throat, palpate the sinuses, check the mucous membranes and capillary refill
steps.find: No signs of head injury. Tympanic membranes normal. Throat mildly red with no exudate. Sinuses not tender. Mucous membranes dry. CRT 2 seconds.

steps.do: Feel the pulse and peripheries, auscultate the heart
steps.find: HR 112 regular. Heart sounds dual, no murmur. Peripheries warm.

steps.do: Inspect and auscultate the chest
steps.find: Chest clear, no wheeze. No increased work of breathing.

steps.do: Palpate the abdomen and check for renal angle tenderness
steps.find: Soft and non-tender. No renal angle tenderness.

bedside.find: 8.6 mmol/L (mildly raised, fits prednisolone and acute illness)

bedside.test: Blood, CT brain and CSF results
bedside.find: Not yet available: the nurse says they will be available in Part 2

amsa-645.key: Ned has fever of 38.9 °C, a tachycardia of 112 and marked neck stiffness with positive Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs, so he has bacterial meningitis until proven otherwise. He is on daily prednisolone, which makes him immunocompromised, so take blood cultures and give dexamethasone and IV antibiotics now, with Listeria cover, without waiting for CT or LP. His GCS of 15, equal pupils, absence of papilloedema and focal signs, and lack of rash are important reassuring negatives: they argue against encephalitis, raised intracranial pressure and meningococcal septicaemia, and they are his baseline for monitoring.

amsa-646.vitals: T 39.0 °C, HR 124/min regular, BP 112/70 mmHg, RR 24/min, SpO2 97% on room air, capillary refill 2 seconds, capillary glucose 5.4 mmol/L, pain 8/10 (practice nurse, on arrival)
amsa-646.general: Unwell and flushed young woman sitting hunched with her eyes half-closed against the light, holding her head still and moving it as little as possible. She speaks quietly and slowly but clearly. Alert and oriented to time, place and person, with normal speech. GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6). No obvious rash on exposed skin. Peripheries warm.

steps.do: Assess GCS and orientation to time, place and person, and observe behaviour and speech
steps.find: GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6). Alert and fully oriented, with normal speech and appropriate behaviour. No confusion or drowsiness.

steps.do: Inspect the whole skin, including trunk, limbs, palms, soles and conjunctivae, for petechiae or purpura, ready to do a glass test on any spots
steps.find: No rash, petechiae or purpura anywhere, including palms, soles and conjunctivae. There are no spots to test with a glass. Peripheries warm, capillary refill 2 seconds.

steps.do: Test passive neck flexion, then Kernig's sign on both sides and Brudzinski's sign
steps.find: Neck stiffness: she resists passive neck flexion and cannot touch her chin to her chest because of pain ("Ow, my neck"). Kernig's sign positive on both sides. Brudzinski's sign positive.

steps.do: Examine both fundi with an ophthalmoscope for papilloedema and haemorrhages
steps.find: Optic discs pink with sharp margins on both sides. No papilloedema. No retinal haemorrhages.

steps.do: Check pupil size and light reflexes, visual fields, eye movements, facial movement and sensation, and screen the other cranial nerves
steps.find: Pupils 4 mm, equal and reactive to light. Visual fields full. Eye movements full with no double vision or nystagmus. Face symmetrical, facial sensation normal. Other cranial nerves normal.

steps.do: Test for pronator drift, then tone, power, reflexes, sensation, plantar responses and coordination
steps.find: No pronator drift. Tone, power (5/5), reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical. Plantars flexor on both sides. Coordination normal.

steps.do: Watch her walk
steps.find: Walks normally but slowly. No ataxia.

steps.area: Ears, nose, throat, sinuses and neck nodes
steps.do: Look in the nose, throat and ears with an otoscope, press over the sinuses and feel the cervical lymph nodes for a source of infection
steps.find: Clear nasal discharge with mild congestion. Throat mildly red with no exudate. Tympanic membranes normal on both sides. Sinuses not tender. No significant cervical lymph nodes.

steps.do: Auscultate the chest and heart
steps.find: Chest clear with no added sounds. Heart sounds dual with no murmur (tachycardic).

steps.do: Palpate both temporal arteries
steps.find: Normal, not tender, pulses present.

bedside.find: 5.4 mmol/L (normal)
The repeat set taken 15 minutes later is handed over in Part 2
Not done in the practice; she must not be delayed for it. To be done in the ED
Take them in the practice only if this does not delay the antibiotic. Otherwise they are taken in the ED

amsa-646.key: Molly has fever (39.0 °C), a fast heart rate (124/min) and fast breathing (24/min). She also has neck stiffness and a positive Kernig's sign on both sides, while being fully alert with GCS 15. Together this means suspected bacterial meningitis with suspected sepsis. She is 18, has just come back from a festival where she shared a tent, and is not sure about her meningococcal vaccines, so meningococcal disease is most likely. She needs a parenteral antibiotic now and an emergency ambulance. The lack of a rash does not exclude meningococcal disease. Her fundi are normal, she has no focal neurological signs and she is not confused, which argues against raised intracranial pressure, encephalitis and a structural cause. Her mild coryza and red throat do not explain the meningism.

amsa-647.vitals: HR 77/min regular, BP 135/85 mmHg, Temp 37.0 °C, RR 15/min, SpO2 99% on room air (practice nurse, on arrival; pain 8/10)
amsa-647.general: A well-looking young woman in obvious pain. She squints in the room light, speaks quietly and holds her head still. Alert and fully orientated. Not pale or flushed. No rash.

steps.do: Check for neck stiffness, perform Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs, and inspect the skin for a rash
steps.find: No neck stiffness. Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs negative. No rash on the skin.

steps.do: Dim the lights and examine both fundi with an ophthalmoscope, looking for papilloedema or haemorrhages
steps.find: She finds the light uncomfortable but cooperates. Both optic discs pink with sharp margins. Spontaneous venous pulsations present. No haemorrhages.

steps.do: Test visual acuity, visual fields to confrontation in each eye, pupils, eyelids and eye movements
steps.find: Visual acuity 6/6 in each eye. Visual fields full to confrontation in each eye. Pupils equal and reactive to light. No ptosis. Eye movements full, with no double vision and no nystagmus.

steps.do: Test facial sensation and movement, speech, palate and tongue
steps.find: Facial sensation and movement normal and symmetrical. Speech normal, with no dysarthria or word-finding difficulty. Palate and tongue normal.

steps.do: Test for pronator drift, then tone, power, reflexes and sensation in all four limbs, and the plantar responses
steps.find: No pronator drift. Tone, power (5/5), reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical in all four limbs. Plantar responses flexor.

steps.do: Finger-nose and heel-shin testing, gait including heel-to-toe walking, and Romberg's test
steps.find: Finger-nose and heel-shin normal. Gait normal, including heel-to-toe walking. Romberg negative.

steps.do: Palpate the temporal arteries, sinuses, scalp, neck muscles and jaw joints
steps.find: Temporal arteries pulsatile and non-tender. Sinuses non-tender. No tenderness of the scalp, neck muscles or jaw joints.

bedside.test: Urine pregnancy test (point of care, practice nurse)
bedside.find: Negative, with a valid control line (the full result is handed over in Part 2)

amsa-647.key: The examination is completely normal. She is afebrile with no meningism, her fundi show sharp discs with venous pulsations (no papilloedema), and there are no focal neurological signs, so there are no red flags for meningitis, raised intracranial pressure, a bleed or a TIA. Together with a gradual onset, a stereotyped pattern and a fully reversible visual aura, this supports migraine with aura managed in general practice without imaging. Her BP of 135/85 was taken while she was in severe pain and needs a repeat, but the combined pill must stop because of the aura whatever her BP.

amsa-663.vitals: HR 84 bpm regular, BP 122/76 mmHg, RR 14 breaths/min, SpO2 99% on room air, temperature 36.9 °C, weight 70 kg (75 kg two months ago), height 178 cm, BMI 22.1 kg/m²
amsa-663.general: Alert, friendly young man, comfortable at rest and not distressed. Slim build. Not pale or jaundiced. Well hydrated: moist mucous membranes, normal skin turgor. Not short of breath. No drip, stoma or other equipment.

steps.do: Inspect the nails and palms for clubbing, palmar pallor, leuconychia and palmar erythema; check capillary refill.
steps.find: No clubbing, no palmar pallor, no leuconychia. Capillary refill under 2 seconds. Normal.

steps.do: Inspect the conjunctivae and sclerae for redness (episcleritis, uveitis), conjunctival pallor and jaundice.
steps.find: No redness or injection, no conjunctival pallor, no scleral icterus. Normal.

steps.do: Inspect the oral mucosa, tongue and gums for aphthous ulcers, angular stomatitis and hydration.
steps.find: No mouth ulcers. Moist mucous membranes. Normal.

steps.do: Expose and inspect the abdomen lying flat for distension, scars, visible masses and stomas.
steps.find: Not distended, no scars, no visible masses. Normal.

steps.do: Palpate lightly then deeply in all nine regions, watching his face; check for guarding and rebound; palpate and percuss for the liver and spleen; ballot the kidneys; check the renal angles.
steps.find: Soft. Mild tenderness in the left iliac fossa, with no guarding or rebound. No masses. Liver and spleen not palpable. Renal angles not tender. Percussion note normal, no shifting dullness.

steps.do: Listen for bowel sounds.
steps.find: Bowel sounds present and normal. Not tinkling, not absent.

steps.do: Expose and inspect both lower legs; palpate any lesions for tenderness, size, warmth and ulceration; look elsewhere for pyoderma gangrenosum.
steps.find: Four tender, raised, red-purple nodules 1 to 3 cm across over both anterior shins, with no ulceration. Consistent with erythema nodosum. No other rashes or skin ulcers.

steps.do: Inspect and palpate the small joints of the hands, the knees and the ankles for swelling, warmth and tenderness.
steps.find: No swelling or tenderness of the hands, knees or ankles. Normal.

steps.do: Auscultate the heart and lung fields.
steps.find: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs. Chest clear with good air entry on both sides. Normal.

steps.area: Perianal inspection and digital rectal examination
steps.do: Explain and get consent, offer a chaperone, position him in the left lateral position; inspect the perianal region, then perform a digital rectal examination and inspect the glove.
steps.find: No skin tags, fissures, fistulae or abscess. Rectum mildly tender, no mass felt. Blood and mucus on the glove.

bedside.find: 70 kg, height 178 cm, BMI 22.1 kg/m². About 5 kg (7%) lost from 75 kg over 2 months.
Lying 122/76 mmHg, HR 84; standing 120/78 mmHg, HR 88. No postural drop, no symptoms.
No blood, protein, leucocytes, nitrites, glucose or ketones. Normal.
5.4 mmol/L (random). Normal.

amsa-663.key: Andy has lost 5 kg, his left iliac fossa is mildly tender, and there is blood and mucus on the glove, with no perianal disease. Together with tender nodules on both shins (erythema nodosum), this points to inflammatory bowel disease affecting the distal bowel, and the absence of skin tags, fissures or fistulae makes Crohn's disease less likely. He has no fever, no tachycardia and no peritonism, is not pale and is well hydrated, so there are no signs of acute severe colitis and he can be investigated and managed as an outpatient.
